title.zh: 卷51 韓茂 皮豹子 封敕文 吕羅漢 孔伯恭
title.en: Volume 51: Han Mao, Pi Baozi, Feng Chiwen, Lu Luohan, Kong Bogong
title.raw: 卷51 韓茂 皮豹子 封敕文 吕羅漢 孔伯恭 Volume 51: Han Mao, Pi Baozi, Feng Chiwen, Lu Luohan, Kong Bogong

sentences.zh: 韓茂 皮豹子 封敕文 呂羅漢 孔伯恭

translations.literal: Han Mao, Pi Baozi, Feng Chiwen, Lu Luohan, Kong Bogong
translations.idiomatic: Han Mao, Pi Baozi, Feng Chiwen, Lu Luohan, and Kong Bogong

sentences.zh: 韓茂，字元興，安定安武人也。

translations.literal: Han Mao, styled Yuanxing, was a man of Anwu in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Han Mao, whose courtesy name was Yuanxing, came from Anwu in Anding Commandery.

sentences.zh: [1]父耆，字黃老。

translations.literal: His father Qi, styled Huanglao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi bore the courtesy name Huanglao.

sentences.zh: 永興中自赫連屈丐來降，拜綏遠將軍，遷龍驤將軍、常山太守，假安武侯。

translations.literal: In the Yongxing era he came down from Helian Quchao to surrender, was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance, was promoted to Dragon-Prancing General and Administrator of Changshan, and was given the acting title Marquis of Anwu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxing period he defected from Helian Quchao, was made General Who Pacifies the Distance, then promoted to Dragon-Prancing General and Administrator of Changshan, with the provisional title Marquis of Anwu.

sentences.zh: 仍居常山之九門。

translations.literal: He continued to reside at Jiumen in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to live at Jiumen in Changshan.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈涇州刺史，諡曰成侯。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Governor of Jing Province, with the posthumous title Marquis Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously appointed Governor of Jing Province and given the posthumous name Marquis Cheng.

sentences.zh: 茂年十七，膂力過人，尤善騎射。

translations.literal: When Mao was seventeen his physical strength surpassed others, and he was especially skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen, Mao possessed extraordinary strength and was especially adept at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 太宗曾親征丁零翟猛，茂為中軍執幢。

translations.literal: The Emperor Daozong once personally campaigned against Zhai Meng of the Dingling; Mao served in the central army bearing the standard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor Daozong personally led a campaign against Zhai Meng of the Dingling, Mao served in the central army as standard-bearer.

sentences.zh: 時有風，諸軍旌旗皆偃仆，茂於馬上持幢，初不傾倒。

translations.literal: There was wind, and the banners of all the armies fell flat; Mao on horseback held the standard and from the first did not let it topple.
translations.idiomatic: A wind arose and every army's banners were blown flat, yet Mao on horseback held his standard upright without it ever swaying.

sentences.zh: 太宗異而問之，徵茂所屬，具以狀對。

translations.literal: The Emperor Daozong was struck by this and inquired; Mao's unit was summoned and reported the matter in full.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor Daozong was astonished and asked about it; Mao's unit was called forward and gave a full account.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂左右曰：「記之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor Daozong said to those beside him, "Record this."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor Daozong told his attendants, "Make a note of that."

sentences.zh: 尋徵詣行在所，試以騎射，太宗深奇之，以茂為虎賁中郎將。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to the imperial camp, tested in mounted archery; the Emperor Daozong was deeply impressed and appointed Mao as Tiger Guard Central Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to the imperial camp and tested in mounted archery; the Emperor Daozong was deeply impressed and appointed Mao Tiger Guard Central Commandant.

sentences.zh: 後從世祖討赫連昌，大破之。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Emperor Taiwu in attacking Helian Chang and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Emperor Taiwu in the campaign against Helian Chang and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 世祖謂諸將曰：「今若窮兵極武，非弔民之道，明年當共卿等取之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor Taiwu said to the generals, "If we now exhaust the army and push warfare to the limit, that is not the way to succor the people; next year we shall take it together with you."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu told his generals, "To press the campaign to extremes now would not be the way to relieve the people; next year we shall take it together with you."

sentences.zh: 徙其民而還。

translations.literal: He relocated the populace and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated the local population and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以軍功賜茂爵蒲陰子，加強弩將軍，遷侍輦郎。

translations.literal: For military merit Mao was granted the title Viscount of Puyin, was made additionally Strong Crossbow General, and was transferred to Attendant of the Imperial Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: For his military achievements Mao was enfeoffed as Viscount of Puyin, given the additional rank of Strong Crossbow General, and promoted to Attendant of the Imperial Carriage.

sentences.zh: 又從征統萬，大破之。

translations.literal: He again followed on the campaign against Tongwan and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He again took part in the campaign against Tongwan and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 從平平涼，當茂所衝，莫不應弦而殪。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Pingliang; wherever Mao charged, none failed to fall the moment the bowstring sounded.
translations.idiomatic: In the pacification of Pingliang, every foe who met Mao's charge fell the instant his bowstring sang.

sentences.zh: 由是世祖壯之，拜內侍長，進爵九門侯，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Because of this the Emperor Taiwu admired him, appointed him Chief Palace Attendant, advanced his rank to Marquis of Jiumen, and made him additionally Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed by this, Emperor Taiwu appointed him Chief Palace Attendant, raised him to Marquis of Jiumen, and gave him the additional title Champion General.

sentences.zh: 後從征蠕蠕，頻戰大捷。

translations.literal: Later he followed campaigns against the Rouran and repeatedly won great victories in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He later campaigned against the Rouran and won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 與樂平王丕等伐和龍，徙其居民。

translations.literal: Together with the Prince of Leping, Pi, and others he attacked Helong and relocated its inhabitants.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Prince Leping Pi and others he attacked Helong and resettled its people.

sentences.zh: 從平涼州，茂為前鋒都將，戰功居多。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Liang Province; Mao served as vanguard commander and his battle achievements were foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In the pacification of Liang Province he served as vanguard commander and accounted for the lion's share of the victories.

sentences.zh: 遷司衞監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 錄前後功，拜散騎常侍、殿中尚書，進爵安定公，加平南將軍。

translations.literal: His past and present achievements were recorded; he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Palace Secretariat Director, advanced to Duke of Anding, and made additionally Pacifier of the South General.
translations.idiomatic: His cumulative achievements were recognized with appointment as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Palace Secretariat Director, elevation to Duke of Anding, and the additional rank of Pacifier of the South General.

sentences.zh: 從破薛永宗，伐蓋吳。

translations.literal: He followed in the defeat of Xue Yongzong and the campaign against Gai Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in defeating Xue Yongzong and campaigning against Gai Wu.

sentences.zh: 轉都官尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 從征懸瓠，頻破賊軍。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Xuanchi and repeatedly defeated the rebel armies.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Xuanchi and repeatedly routed the enemy forces.

sentences.zh: 車駕南征，分為六道，茂與高涼王那出青州。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, the forces were divided into six routes; Mao and the Prince of Gaoliang, Na, issued from Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign the army was split into six columns; Mao and Prince Gaoliang Na advanced from Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 諸軍渡淮，降者相繼，拜茂徐州刺史以撫之。

translations.literal: The armies crossed the Huai; surrenderers came in succession, and Mao was appointed Governor of Xu Province to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: After the armies crossed the Huai, surrenders came one after another, and Mao was appointed Governor of Xu Province to oversee their pacification.

sentences.zh: 車駕還，以茂為侍中、尚書左僕射，加征南將軍。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, Mao was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and was given additionally the title Southern Campaign General.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, Mao was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, with the additional rank of Southern Campaign General.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，劉義隆遣將檀和之寇濟州，南安王余令茂討之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Taiwu died, Liu Yilong sent the general Tan Hezhi to raid Ji Province; the Prince of Nan'an, Yu, ordered Mao to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Taiwu's death, Liu Yilong sent General Tan Hezhi to raid Ji Province; Prince Nan'an Yu ordered Mao to repel him.

sentences.zh: 至濟州，和之遁走。

translations.literal: When he reached Ji Province, Hezhi fled.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Ji Province, Hezhi fled without a fight.

sentences.zh: 高宗踐阼，拜尚書令，加侍中、征南大將軍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Wencheng ascended the throne, Mao was appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat and was given additionally Attendant-in-Ordinary and Great General Who Campaigns South.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng took the throne, Mao was made Director of the Imperial Secretariat, with the additional titles of Attendant-in-Ordinary and Great General Who Campaigns South.

sentences.zh: 茂沉毅篤實，雖無文學，每論議合理。

translations.literal: Mao was deep, resolute, and sincere; though without literary learning, his every discussion and deliberation was reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was grave, steadfast, and utterly reliable; though no scholar, his counsel in council was always sound.

sentences.zh: 為將，善於撫眾，勇冠當世，為朝廷所稱。

translations.literal: As a general he was skilled at comforting the troops; his courage topped his age and he was praised by the court.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander he excelled at winning the loyalty of his men; his courage was unrivaled in his day, and the court spoke highly of him.

sentences.zh: 太安二年夏，領太子少師，冬卒。

translations.literal: In summer of the second year of Taian he held the post of Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; in winter he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year of Taian he was appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; he died that winter.

sentences.zh: 贈涇州刺史、安定王，諡曰桓王。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Governor of Jing Province and Prince of Anding, with the posthumous title Prince Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Governor of Jing Province and Prince of Anding, with the posthumous name Prince Huan.

sentences.zh: 長子備，字延德。

translations.literal: His eldest son Bei, styled Yande.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Bei bore the courtesy name Yande.

sentences.zh: 初為中散，賜爵江陽男，加揚烈將軍。

translations.literal: At first he was a Palace Scribe; he was granted the title Baron of Jiangyang and was made additionally Yanglie General.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Palace Scribe, was enfeoffed as Baron of Jiangyang, and given the additional rank of Yanglie General.

sentences.zh: 又進爵行唐侯，拜冠軍將軍、太子庶子。

translations.literal: He was further advanced to Marquis of Xingtang, appointed Champion General and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was further raised to Marquis of Xingtang and appointed Champion General and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 遷寧西將軍，典遊獵曹，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Pacifier of the West General, directed the Hunting Office, and was made additionally Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Pacifier of the West General, put in charge of the Hunting Office, and given the additional title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 襲爵安定公、征南大將軍。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Duke of Anding and Great General Who Campaigns South.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's titles as Duke of Anding and Great General Who Campaigns South.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈雍州刺史，諡曰簡公。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Governor of Yong Province, with the posthumous title Duke Jian.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously appointed Governor of Yong Province and given the posthumous name Duke Jian.

sentences.zh: 備弟均，字天德。

translations.literal: Bei's younger brother Jun, styled Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: Bei's younger brother Jun bore the courtesy name Tiande.

sentences.zh: 少而善射，有將略。

translations.literal: From youth he was skilled at archery and possessed military stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was an expert archer and showed real military talent.

sentences.zh: 初為中散，賜爵范陽子，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: At first he was a Palace Scribe; he was granted the title Viscount of Fanyang and was made additionally Pacifier of the North General.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Palace Scribe, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Fanyang, and given the additional rank of Pacifier of the North General.

sentences.zh: 遷金部尚書，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Treasury and was made additionally Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of the Treasury and given the additional title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 兄備卒，無子，均襲爵安定公、征南大將軍。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Bei died without a son, Jun inherited the titles Duke of Anding and Great General Who Campaigns South.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Bei died childless, Jun inherited the titles of Duke of Anding and Great General Who Campaigns South.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節、散騎常侍、本將軍、定州刺史，轉青冀二州刺史，餘如故。

translations.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, his former general's title, and Governor of Ding Province; he was transferred to Governor of Qing and Ji provinces, his other titles remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and Governor of Ding Province, retaining his general's rank; he was later transferred to govern Qing and Ji provinces while keeping his other titles.

sentences.zh: 恤民廉謹，甚有治稱。

translations.literal: He was compassionate toward the people, incorrupt and prudent, and had a great reputation for governance.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for the people, governed with integrity and restraint, and won wide renown as an administrator.

sentences.zh: 廣阿澤在定、冀、相三州之界，土廣民稀，多有寇盜，乃置鎮以靜之。

translations.literal: Guang'a Marsh lay on the border of Ding, Ji, and Xiang provinces; the land was broad and the people sparse, and there were many bandits and robbers, so a garrison was established to pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: Guang'a Marsh straddled the borders of Ding, Ji, and Xiang provinces, where sparse settlement bred rampant banditry; a military garrison was therefore established to restore order.

sentences.zh: 以均在冀州，劫盜止息，除本將軍、廣阿鎮大將，加都督三州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Because Jun was in Ji Province, robbery and plunder ceased; he was relieved of his former general's title and made Great General of Guang'a Garrison, with the additional post of Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the three provinces.
translations.idiomatic: With Jun governing Ji Province, banditry came to a halt; he was appointed Great General of Guang'a Garrison and given overall military command of the three provinces.

sentences.zh: 均清身率下，明為耳目，廣設方略，禁斷姦邪，於是趙郡屠各、西山丁零聚黨山澤以劫害為業者，均皆誘慰追捕，遠近震跼。

translations.literal: Jun kept his person pure and led his subordinates by example, made himself clear eyes and ears, broadly set forth stratagems, and forbade and cut off wickedness; thus the Tuge of Zhao commandery and the Dingling of the western hills who had gathered in bands in mountains and marshes and made robbery their trade—Jun by inducement, comfort, and pursuit captured them all, and near and far were shaken and constrained.
translations.idiomatic: Jun led by personal example, kept a sharp intelligence network, devised far-reaching plans, and ruthlessly suppressed crime; the Tuge of Zhao and the western Dingling who had banded together in the hills to live by plunder were one after another lured, pacified, or hunted down, and the whole region trembled at his authority.

sentences.zh: 先是，河外未賓，民多去就，故權立東青州為招懷之本，新附之民，咸受優復。

translations.literal: Previously, the lands beyond the river had not submitted; the people often went back and forth, so provisionally Eastern Qing Province was established as a base for winning hearts, and all newly attached people received favorable exemptions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because the territory south of the Yellow River had not yet submitted and the population moved freely between regimes, the court had provisionally established Eastern Qing Province as a base for winning allegiance, granting favorable tax exemptions to all who newly submitted.

sentences.zh: 然舊人姦逃者，多往投焉。

translations.literal: Yet old subjects who were wicked fugitives mostly went to throw themselves in there.
translations.idiomatic: Yet many longtime subjects who had fled justice took refuge there instead.

sentences.zh: 均表陳非便，朝議罷之。

translations.literal: Jun memorialized stating it was not advantageous; the court deliberated and abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: Jun submitted a memorial arguing the arrangement was harmful; the court agreed and abolished the province.

sentences.zh: 後均所統，劫盜頗起，顯祖詔書誚讓之。

translations.literal: Later in the territory Jun commanded, robbery and plunder arose considerably; the Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict reproaching him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, banditry flared again in the territory under Jun's command, and Emperor Xiaowen sent an edict of rebuke.

sentences.zh: 又以五州民戶殷多，編籍不實，以均忠直不阿，詔均檢括，出十餘萬戶。

translations.literal: Also, because in the five provinces households were numerous and the registers were not accurate, and because Jun was loyal, upright, and did not flatter, the emperor ordered Jun to inspect and tally, uncovering more than a hundred thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Because the five provinces were densely populated yet their household registers were grossly inaccurate, and because Jun was known for his integrity and refusal to curry favor, the emperor ordered him to conduct a census audit that uncovered more than a hundred thousand unregistered households.

sentences.zh: 復授定州刺史，輕徭寬賦，百姓安之。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Governor of Ding Province; he lightened corvée and broadened tax levies, and the common people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Governor of Ding Province, where he eased corvée labor and lightened taxes until the people lived in contentment.

sentences.zh: 延興五年卒，諡曰康公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yanxing he died, with the posthumous title Duke Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Yanxing and was given the posthumous name Duke Kang.

sentences.zh: 子寶石襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Baoshi inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoshi inherited the family title.

sentences.zh: 均弟天生，為內廐令，後典龍牧曹。

translations.literal: Jun's younger brother Tiansheng served as Director of the Inner Stud and later directed the Dragon Herds Office.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's younger brother Tiansheng served as Director of the Inner Stud and later oversaw the Dragon Herds Office.

sentences.zh: 出為持節、平北將軍、沃野鎮將。

translations.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff, Pacifier of the North General, and Commander of Woye Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Pacifier of the North General, and commander of Woye Garrison.

sentences.zh: 皮豹子，漁陽人。

translations.literal: Pi Baozi was a man of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pi Baozi came from Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 少有武略。

translations.literal: From youth he had military stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he showed military talent.

sentences.zh: 泰常中，為中散，稍遷內侍左右。

translations.literal: In the Taichang era he was a Palace Scribe and was gradually promoted to Attendant of the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taichang period he served as a Palace Scribe and was gradually promoted to Attendant of the Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，為散騎常侍，賜爵新安侯，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the time of the Emperor Taiwu he was Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, was granted the title Marquis of Xin'an, and was made additionally Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taiwu he served as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xin'an, and given the additional rank of Champion General.

sentences.zh: 又拜選部尚書，餘如故。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Minister of Personnel, his other titles remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed Minister of Personnel while retaining his other titles.

sentences.zh: 出除使持節、侍中、都督秦雍荊梁四州諸軍事、安西將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵淮陽公，鎮長安。

translations.literal: He went out and was relieved to serve as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Qin, Yong, Jing, and Liang provinces, Pacifier of the West General, with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, was advanced to Duke of Huaiyang, and garrisoned Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched as Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Attendant-in-Ordinary, with supreme military command over Qin, Yong, Jing, and Liang provinces, as Pacifier of the West General with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies; he was raised to Duke of Huaiyang and stationed at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 尋加征西將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was given additionally the title Western Campaign General.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the additional rank of Western Campaign General.

sentences.zh: 後坐盜官財，徙於統萬。

translations.literal: Later he was convicted of embezzling official property and was banished to Tongwan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later convicted of embezzling government funds and exiled to Tongwan.

sentences.zh: 真君三年，劉義隆遣將裴方明等侵南秦王楊難當，遂陷仇池。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenjun, Liu Yilong sent the generals Pei Fangming and others to invade the Southern Qin king Yang Nandang, and they thereupon took Qiu Pool.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenjun, Liu Yilong sent Generals Pei Fangming and others against the Southern Qin ruler Yang Nandang, and they captured Qiu Pool.

sentences.zh: 世祖徵豹子，復其爵位。

translations.literal: The Emperor Taiwu summoned Baozi and restored his title and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu recalled Baozi and restored his titles.

sentences.zh: 尋拜使持節、仇池鎮將，督關中諸軍，與建興公古弼等分命諸將，十道並進。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Commander of Qiu Pool Garrison, supervising all armies in Guanzhong; together with the Duke of Jianxing, Gu Bi, and others he assigned orders to the generals, and ten columns advanced together.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Bearer of the Staff and commander of Qiu Pool Garrison with authority over all Guanzhong forces; together with Duke Jianxing Gu Bi and others he divided the army into ten columns that advanced simultaneously.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，豹子進擊樂鄉，大破之，擒義隆將王奐之、王長卿等六人，斬首三千餘級，俘獲二千人。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, Baozi advanced and attacked Leyang, inflicting a great defeat; he captured Liu Yilong's generals Wang Huanzhi, Wang Changqing, and six others in all, beheaded more than three thousand, and took two thousand prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year, Baozi attacked Leyang and won a crushing victory, capturing six of Liu Yilong's generals including Wang Huanzhi and Wang Changqing, taking more than three thousand heads, and making two thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 豹子進軍下辨，義隆將強玄明、辛伯奮棄城遁走，追斬之，悉獲其眾。

translations.literal: Baozi advanced his army to Xiabian; Liu Yilong's generals Qiang Xuanming and Xin Bofen abandoned the city and fled; he pursued and beheaded them and took all their troops.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi marched on Xiabian; Liu Yilong's generals Qiang Xuanming and Xin Bofen abandoned the city and fled, but he pursued and killed them and captured their entire force.

sentences.zh: 義隆使其秦州刺史胡崇之鎮仇池，至漢中，聞官軍已西，懼不敢進，方明益其兵而遣之。

translations.literal: Yilong sent his Governor of Qin Province, Hu Chongzhi, to garrison Qiu Pool; when he reached Hanzhong and heard the government armies had already gone west, he was afraid and did not dare advance; Fangming reinforced his troops and sent him on.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong sent his Governor of Qin, Hu Chongzhi, to hold Qiu Pool; when Hu reached Hanzhong and learned that the imperial armies had already marched west, he was too frightened to advance, so Fangming reinforced his troops and sent him forward again.

sentences.zh: 豹子與司馬楚之至於濁水，擊擒崇之，盡虜其眾。

translations.literal: Baozi and Sima Chu reached Zhuoshui, attacked and captured Chongzhi, and took all his troops prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi and Sima Chu reached Zhuoshui, defeated and captured Chongzhi, and took his entire army prisoner.

sentences.zh: 進至高平，義隆將姜道祖降，仇池平。

translations.literal: Advancing to Gaoping, Liu Yilong's general Jiang Daozu surrendered, and Qiu Pool was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Gaoping, they accepted the surrender of Liu Yilong's general Jiang Daozu, and Qiu Pool was pacified.

sentences.zh: 未幾，諸氐復反，推楊文德為主以圍仇池。

translations.literal: Before long the various Di rebelled again, set up Yang Wende as leader, and besieged Qiu Pool.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Di tribes rebelled again, enthroned Yang Wende as their leader, and laid siege to Qiu Pool.

sentences.zh: 古弼率諸軍討平之。

translations.literal: Gu Bi led the armies to campaign and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Bi led the armies to suppress the rebellion and restore order.

sentences.zh: 時豹子次于下辨，聞圍解，欲還。

translations.literal: At the time Baozi was encamped at Xiabian; hearing the siege was lifted, he wished to return.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi was then stationed at Xiabian; when he heard the siege had been lifted, he prepared to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 弼遣使謂豹子曰：「賊耻其負敗，必求報復，後舉為難，不如陳兵以待之。」

translations.literal: Bi sent a messenger to say to Baozi, "The rebels are shamed by their defeat and loss; they will surely seek revenge. If they rise later it will be trouble—better to array the troops and wait for them."
translations.idiomatic: Bi sent a messenger telling Baozi, "The enemy are humiliated by their defeat and will surely seek revenge; if we withdraw now they will strike again when we least expect it. Better to hold our position and wait for them."

sentences.zh: 豹子以為然。

translations.literal: Baozi considered this right.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋除都督秦、雍、荊、梁、益五州諸軍事，進號征西大將軍，開府、仇池鎮將、持節、公如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was relieved to serve as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Qin, Yong, Jing, Liang, and Yi provinces, was advanced in title to Great General Who Campaigns West, and his privileges of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, command of Qiu Pool Garrison, Bearer of the Staff, and ducal rank remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed supreme commander of military affairs in Qin, Yong, Jing, Liang, and Yi provinces, promoted to Great General Who Campaigns West, while retaining his privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, his command of Qiu Pool Garrison, the Staff of Authority, and his ducal title.

sentences.zh: 十一月，義隆復遣楊文德、姜道盛率眾二萬人寇濁水，別遣將青陽顯伯守斧山以拒豹子。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Yilong again sent Yang Wende and Jiang Daosheng leading twenty thousand men to raid Zhuoshui, and separately sent the general Qingyang Xianbo to hold Fushan to resist Baozi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Yilong again sent Yang Wende and Jiang Daosheng with twenty thousand men against Zhuoshui, while dispatching General Qingyang Xianbo to hold Fushan and block Baozi's advance.

sentences.zh: 濁水城兵射殺道盛，豹子至斧山，斬顯伯，悉俘其眾。

translations.literal: The troops of Zhuoshui city shot and killed Daosheng; Baozi reached Fushan, beheaded Xianbo, and took all his troops prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison at Zhuoshui shot and killed Daosheng; Baozi then reached Fushan, killed Xianbo, and captured his entire force.

sentences.zh: 豹子又與河間公元齊俱會于濁水，賊眾震恐，棄其兵甲夜遁。

translations.literal: Baozi again joined the Prince of Hejian, Yuan Qi, at Zhuoshui; the rebel masses were shaken with terror, abandoned their arms and armor, and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi joined Prince Hejian Yuan Qi at Zhuoshui; the enemy army was seized with panic, abandoned their weapons, and fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 初，南秦王楊難當歸命，詔送楊氏子弟詣京師，文德以行賂得留，亡奔漢中。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Southern Qin king Yang Nandang submitted, an edict ordered the Yang clan's sons and younger brothers sent to the capital; Wende by bribery obtained permission to remain, fled, and went to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Southern Qin ruler Yang Nandang had earlier submitted, the court ordered the Yang clan's younger members sent to the capital; Wende bribed his way into staying behind, then fled to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 義隆以文德為武都王，給兵二千人守葭蘆城，招誘氐羌，於是武都、陰平五部氐民叛應文德。

translations.literal: Yilong made Wende Prince of Wudu, gave him two thousand troops to garrison Jialu City, and recruited and enticed the Di and Qiang; thereupon the Di people of the five divisions of Wudu and Yinping rebelled and responded to Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong made Wende Prince of Wudu, gave him two thousand troops to hold Jialu City, and set him to win over the Di and Qiang; the five Di divisions of Wudu and Yinping thereupon rose in rebellion to join him.

sentences.zh: 詔豹子率諸軍討之，文德阻兵固險拒豹子。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Baozi to lead the armies to campaign against him; Wende blocked the troops and held the passes firm to resist Baozi.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Baozi to lead the armies against him; Wende used his terrain and troops to block Baozi's advance.

sentences.zh: 文德將楊高來降，引諸軍向其城，文德棄城南走，收其妻子、僚屬、軍資及故武都王保宗妻公主送京師。

translations.literal: Wende's general Yang Gao came to surrender, led the armies toward his city; Wende abandoned the city and fled south; they gathered his wife and children, staff, military stores, and the former Prince of Wudu Baozong's wife the princess and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wende's general Yang Gao defected and guided the imperial armies to the city; Wende abandoned it and fled south; Baozi's forces seized Wende's family, officials, military supplies, and the former Prince of Wudu Baozong's wife the princess, and sent them all to the capital.

sentences.zh: 義隆白水太守郭啟玄率眾救文德，豹子分軍逆擊，大破之，啟玄、文德走還漢中。

translations.literal: Liu Yilong's Administrator of Baishui, Guo Qixuan, led troops to rescue Wende; Baozi divided his army and struck them head-on, inflicting a great defeat; Qixuan and Wende fled back to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yilong's Administrator of Baishui, Guo Qixuan, marched to relieve Wende; Baozi split his forces and met them head-on, winning a crushing victory; Qixuan and Wende fled back to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 興安二年正月，義隆遣其將蕭道成、王虬、馬光等入漢中，別令楊文德、楊頭等率諸氐羌圍武都。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Xing'an, Yilong sent his generals Xiao Daocheng, Wang Qiu, Ma Guang, and others into Hanzhong, and separately ordered Yang Wende, Yang Tou, and others to lead the various Di and Qiang to besiege Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Xing'an, Yilong sent Generals Xiao Daocheng, Wang Qiu, Ma Guang, and others into Hanzhong, while separately ordering Yang Wende, Yang Tou, and others to lead the Di and Qiang in a siege of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 城中拒之，殺賊二百餘人。

translations.literal: The city resisted them and killed more than two hundred of the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders held the city and killed more than two hundred of the besiegers.

sentences.zh: 豹子分兵將救之，至女磊，聞賊停軍，豹子遣人於祁山取馬，欲往赴援。

translations.literal: Baozi divided his troops to go rescue them; when he reached Nülei he heard the rebels had halted their army; Baozi sent men to Qishan to fetch horses, intending to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi detached a force to relieve the siege; reaching Nülei, he learned the enemy had halted; he sent men to Qishan to fetch horses, preparing to march to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 文德謂豹子欲斷其糧運，回軍還入覆津，據險自固。

translations.literal: Wende thought Baozi intended to cut off his grain transport, turned his army back and entered into Fu Ford, and held the passes firm to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wende concluded that Baozi meant to cut his supply lines, withdrew into Fu Ford, and fortified the difficult terrain.

sentences.zh: 義隆恐其輒回，又增兵益將，令晉壽、白水送糧覆津，漢川、武興運粟甘泉，皆置倉儲。

translations.literal: Yilong feared he might return at once, again increased troops and reinforced generals, ordered Jinshou and Baishui to send grain to Fu Ford, and Hanchuan and Wuxing to transport grain to Ganquan, all establishing storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Wende might retreat prematurely, Yilong reinforced the army and ordered Jinshou and Baishui to ship grain to Fu Ford and Hanchuan and Wuxing to transport grain to Ganquan, establishing depots at each point.

sentences.zh: 豹子表曰：「義隆增兵運糧，剋必送死。

translations.literal: Baozi memorialized, saying, "Yilong is increasing troops and transporting grain; when we attack, they will surely come to die.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi submitted a memorial: "Yilong is reinforcing and building up supplies; when we strike, his men will fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 臣所領之眾，本自不多，唯仰民兵，專恃防固。

translations.literal: The troops I command were from the first not numerous; I rely solely on local militia and depend exclusively on defensive fortification.
translations.idiomatic: The force under my command was never large to begin with; I rely entirely on local militia and can only hold defensive positions.

sentences.zh: 其統萬、安定二鎮之眾，從戎以來，經三四歲，長安之兵，役過期月，未有代期，衣糧俱盡，形顏枯悴，窘切戀家，逃亡不已，既臨寇難，不任攻戰。

translations.literal: As for the masses of the two garrisons of Tongwan and Anding, since joining the campaign they have passed three or four years; the troops from Chang'an have served beyond the term of their corvée by a full month, with no set time for replacement; clothing and provisions are utterly exhausted, their faces haggard and wasted, in dire straits and longing for home, fleeing without cease; now facing bandit raiders, they cannot bear offensive warfare.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison forces at Tongwan and Anding have been on campaign for three or four years; the troops from Chang'an have already exceeded their term of service by a month with no replacement in sight; their clothing and rations are gone, they are gaunt and homesick, and desertion is constant—they can no longer fight when the enemy comes.

sentences.zh: 士民姦通，知臣兵弱，南引文德，共為脣齒。

translations.literal: Local gentry and commoners collude treacherously; knowing my troops are weak, they summon Wende from the south, and together act as lip and teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Local elites and commoners are in secret collusion; knowing my forces are weak, they appeal to Wende in the south, and the two sides work together like lips and teeth.

sentences.zh: 計文德去年八月與義隆梁州刺史劉秀之同征長安，聞臺遣大軍，勢援雲集，長安地平，用馬為便，畏國騎軍，不敢北出。

translations.literal: I reckon that last year in the eighth month Wende jointly attacked Chang'an with Yilong's Inspector of Liang Province Liu Xiuzhi; hearing the court had dispatched a great army with supports gathering like clouds, and that the Chang'an plain is level ground suited to horses, he feared our national cavalry and did not dare advance north.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that last August Wende joined Yilong's Liang Province Inspector Liu Xiuzhi in an attack on Chang'an; when he heard the court was sending a large army and reinforcements were massing, and knowing the flat terrain around Chang'an favors cavalry, he feared our mounted forces and did not dare march north.

sentences.zh: 但承仇池局人，[2]稱臺軍不多，戍兵尠少，諸州雜人，各有還思，軍勢若及，必自奔逃，進軍取城，有易返掌。

translations.literal: Yet relying on a local contact at Qiu Pool, [2] who said the court's army was not numerous, garrison troops few, and mixed populations from the various provinces each harbored thoughts of returning home—if our military power reached them they would surely flee of themselves; advancing the army to take the city would be as easy as turning one's palm.
translations.idiomatic: But taking word from a contact at Qiu Pool, [2] he was told the imperial army was small, garrisons thinly manned, and troops from various provinces all wanted to go home—once our forces arrived they would surely run; capturing the city would be effortless.

sentences.zh: 承信其語，回趣長安之兵，遣文德、蕭道成、王虬等將領，來攻武都、仇池，望連秦隴。

translations.literal: Believing this talk, he turned the Chang'an troops back and sent generals Wende, Xiao Daocheng, Wang Qiu, and others to attack Wudu and Qiu Pool, hoping to link Qin and Long.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting this report, he redirected the Chang'an force and sent Wende, Xiao Daocheng, Wang Qiu, and other commanders to strike Wudu and Qiu Pool, aiming to join Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 進圍武都，已經積日，畏臣截後，斷其糧路，關鎮少兵，未有大損。

translations.literal: They advanced and besieged Wudu for many days already; fearing I would cut behind them and sever their grain route, with few troops in the passes and garrisons, they have not suffered great loss.
translations.idiomatic: They have besieged Wudu for many days, but fear I will cut off their retreat and grain supply; the frontier posts have few troops, so we have not yet suffered heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 今外寇兵強，臣力寡弱，拒賊備敵，非兵不擬，乞選壯兵，增戍武都，牢城自守，可以無患。

translations.literal: Now the outer bandits' troops are strong while my strength is few and weak; to resist bandits and guard against the enemy, I cannot match them without troops; I beg that sturdy soldiers be selected to reinforce the garrison at Wudu, hold the city firm in self-defense, and thus be free from worry.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is strong and my force is weak; we cannot hold them off without more men. I ask that strong troops be selected to reinforce Wudu so we can hold the city securely and avoid disaster.

sentences.zh: 今事已切急，若不馳聞，損失城鎮，恐招深責。

translations.literal: The matter is now urgently pressing; if I do not report at speed, losing cities and garrison posts would invite severe rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: The situation is critical; if I fail to report immediately, the loss of cities and posts may bring severe censure upon me.

sentences.zh: 願遣高平突騎二千，賫糧一月，速赴仇池。

translations.literal: I wish that two thousand shock cavalry from Gaoping be sent, carrying one month's grain, hurrying to Qiu Pool.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that two thousand shock cavalry from Gaoping be dispatched with one month's rations and sent swiftly to Qiu Pool.

sentences.zh: 且可抑折逆民，支對賊虜。

translations.literal: Moreover, they could suppress and break the rebellious populace and confront the bandit foe.
translations.idiomatic: They could also cow the disloyal locals and hold the enemy at bay.

sentences.zh: 須長

translations.literal: must wait long
translations.idiomatic: We must wait a considerable time

translations.literal: 〈lacuna〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Text missing in the source.〉

sentences.zh: 、上邽、安定戍兵至，[3]可得自全。

translations.literal: , [and for] Shanggui and Anding garrison troops to arrive, [3] then one can preserve oneself.
translations.idiomatic: For the Shanggui and Anding garrison troops to arrive—[3] only then can we save ourselves.

sentences.zh: 糧者，民之命也，雖有金城湯池，無糧不守。

translations.literal: Grain is the people's very life; though one have a city of metal walls and moats of boiling water, without grain it cannot be held.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions are the lifeblood of the people; even a fortress of iron cannot be held without food.

sentences.zh: 仇池本無儲積，今歲不收，苦高平騎至，[4]不知云何以得供援。

translations.literal: Qiu Pool originally had no stored reserves; this year's harvest failed; if Gaoping cavalry should arrive, [4] I know not how supplies for relief could be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Pool has no stored grain, and this year's harvest failed; even if the Gaoping cavalry arrive, [4] I do not see how supplies can be provided.

sentences.zh: 請遣秦州之民，送軍祁山，臣隨迎致。」

translations.literal: I request that the people of Qin Province be sent to convey the army's grain to Qishan, and I will follow to receive and deliver it."
translations.idiomatic: Please send men from Qin Province to transport grain for the army to Qishan; I will meet them and escort the supplies in."

sentences.zh: 詔高平鎮將苟莫于率突騎二千以赴之，道成等乃退。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Gou Moyu, commander of Gaoping Garrison, to lead two thousand shock cavalry to go to their aid; Daocheng and the others then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Gou Moyu, commander of the Gaoping garrison, to lead two thousand shock cavalry to the rescue; Daocheng and his allies then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 徵豹子為尚書，出為內都大官。

translations.literal: Baozi was summoned to the post of Master of Writing and then sent out as Grand Intendant of the Inner Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi was recalled to serve as Master of Writing, then appointed Grand Intendant of the Inner Capital.

sentences.zh: 劉駿遣其將殷孝祖修兩當城於清東以逼南境，天水公封敕文擊之，不克。

translations.literal: Liu Jun sent his general Yin Xiaozu to repair Liangdang city east of Qing to press the southern frontier; Feng Chiwen, Duke of Tianshui, attacked them but could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun sent General Yin Xiaozu to fortify Liangdang east of Qing, threatening our southern border; Feng Chiwen, Duke of Tianshui, attacked but failed to break them.

sentences.zh: 詔豹子與給事中周丘等助擊之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Baozi, together with Palace Attendant Zhou Qiu and others, to assist in the attack.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Baozi, along with Palace Attendant Zhou Qiu and others, to join the assault.

sentences.zh: 豹子以南寇城守，攻圍費日，遂略地至高平。

translations.literal: Because the southern invaders held the city in defense, the siege consumed days; then he overran territory as far as Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: The southern enemy held the city stubbornly and the siege dragged on for days before Baozi pushed forward as far as Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 劉駿瑕丘鎮遣步卒五千助戍兩當，去城八里，與豹子前鋒候騎相遇，即便交戰，豹子軍繼至，大破之。

translations.literal: Liu Jun's Xiqiu garrison sent five thousand foot soldiers to help garrison Liangdang; eight li from the city they met Baozi's advance scouting cavalry and at once joined battle; Baozi's army followed up and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun's Xiqiu garrison sent five thousand infantry to reinforce Liangdang; eight li from the city they ran into Baozi's advance scouts and fighting broke out at once; Baozi's main force arrived and routed them.

sentences.zh: 縱騎追擊殺之，至於城下，其免者十餘人而已。

translations.literal: He unleashed cavalry in pursuit, killing them down to the city wall; those who escaped numbered barely more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: He sent cavalry in pursuit, slaughtering them all the way to the city walls; barely a dozen men escaped.

sentences.zh: 城內恐懼，不敢出救。

translations.literal: Inside the city, in fear, they did not dare sally out to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison was terrified and dared not sally out to help.

sentences.zh: 既而班師。

translations.literal: Thereupon he withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew his forces.

sentences.zh: 先是，河西諸胡，亡匿避命。

translations.literal: Earlier, the various Hu of Hexi had gone into hiding to evade corvée and taxation.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, various non-Han peoples of Hexi had gone into hiding to evade service and taxes.

sentences.zh: 豹子及前涇州刺史封阿君督河西諸軍南趣石樓，與衞大將軍、樂安王良以討羣胡。

translations.literal: Baozi and the former Inspector of Jing Province Feng Ajun commanded the Hexi armies south toward Shilou, together with Guardian General, Prince of Le'an, Liang, to suppress the Hu bands.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi and former Jing Province Inspector Feng Ajun led the Hexi armies south toward Shilou, joining Guardian General Prince Liang of Le'an to pacify the Hu rebels.

sentences.zh: 豹子等與賊相對，不覺胡走，無捷而還，又坐免官。

translations.literal: Baozi and the others faced the bandits in stalemate, unaware the Hu had fled; returning without victory, they were again punished by dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi and his colleagues camped opposite the rebels but failed to notice the Hu had slipped away; returning without a victory, they were once again stripped of their posts.

sentences.zh: 尋以前後戰功，復擢為內都大官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on account of earlier and later military merit, he was again promoted to Grand Intendant of the Inner Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, in recognition of his accumulated battlefield achievements, he was reappointed Grand Intendant of the Inner Capital.

sentences.zh: 和平五年六月，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Heping, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of the fifth year of Heping.

sentences.zh: 高宗追惜之，贈淮陽王，諡曰襄，賜命服一襲。

translations.literal: Emperor Wencheng mourned and regretted his loss, posthumously enfeoffing him as Prince of Huaiyang with the posthumous title Xiang, and bestowed one set of court robes of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng deeply mourned his passing, posthumously ennobling him as Prince of Huaiyang with the posthumous name Xiang, and granted him a full set of ceremonial robes.

sentences.zh: 子道明，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Daoming inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daoming succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 道明第八弟喜。

translations.literal: Daoming's eighth younger brother Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Daoming's eighth younger brother was Xi.

sentences.zh: 高宗以其名臣子，擢為侍御中散，遷侍御長。

translations.literal: Emperor Wencheng, because he was the son of a noted minister, promoted him to Central Palace Attendant and later transferred him to Chief Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng, recognizing him as the son of a distinguished minister, appointed him Central Palace Attendant and later promoted him to Chief Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，吐谷渾拾寅部落飢窘，侵掠澆河，[5]大為民患。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, the tribes of Tuyuhun's Shibin, hungry and destitute, raided Jiao River, [5] greatly harming the people.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign, the Tuyuhun chieftain Shibin's tribes, starving and desperate, raided the Jiao River region, [5] causing widespread harm to the populace.

sentences.zh: 詔假喜平西將軍、廣川公，領涼州、枹罕、高平諸軍，與上黨王長孫觀討拾寅。

translations.literal: An edict provisionally appointed Xi General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Guangchuan, put him in command of the armies of Liang Province, Fuhan, and Gaoping, and together with the Prince of Shangdang, Zhangsun Guan, marched against Shibin.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Xi acting General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Guangchuan, placing him in command of forces from Liang Province, Fuhan, and Gaoping to campaign against Shibin alongside Prince Zhangsun Guan of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 又拜為使持節、侍中、都督秦雍荊梁益五州諸軍事、本將軍、開府、仇池鎮將，假公如故，以其父豹子昔鎮仇池有威信故也。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the Five Provinces of Qin, Yong, Jing, Liang, and Yi, with his former generalship, with the establishment of a headquarters, and as Commander of Qiu Pool Garrison—the acting ducal title continuing as before—because his father Baozi had once garrisoned Qiu Pool and possessed authority and trust.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, and commander of military affairs across Qin, Yong, Jing, Liang, and Yi, retaining his previous general's rank with headquarters and appointment as garrison commander of Qiu Pool, his acting ducal title unchanged—for his father Baozi had once held Qiu Pool and enjoyed great prestige there.

sentences.zh: 喜至，申恩布惠，夷民大悅，酋帥強奴子等各率戶歸附，於是置廣業、固道二郡以居之。

translations.literal: When Xi arrived, he proclaimed grace and spread kindness; the barbarians and common people were greatly pleased; chieftains such as Qiangnuzi each led their households to submit; thereupon the two commanderies of Guangye and Gudao were established to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi arrived, he showed clemency and generosity; the frontier peoples were overjoyed, and chieftains such as Qiangnuzi led their clans to submit; the court then established Guangye and Gudao commanderies to resettle them.

sentences.zh: 徵為南部尚書，賜爵南康侯，加左將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as Minister of the Southern Bureau, enfeoffed as Marquis of Nankang, and promoted to General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Minister of the Southern Bureau, ennobled as Marquis of Nankang, and promoted to General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 太和元年，劉準葭蘆戍主楊文度遣弟鼠竊據仇池，詔喜率眾四萬討鼠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe, Yang Wendu, commandant of the Jialu garrison under Liu Zhun, sent his brother Shu to seize Qiu Pool by stealth; an edict ordered Xi to lead forty thousand men to subdue Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taihe, Yang Wendu, Liu Zhun's garrison commander at Jialu, sent his brother Shu to seize Qiu Pool; the court ordered Xi to lead forty thousand troops against him.

sentences.zh: 軍到建安，鼠棄城南走。

translations.literal: When the army reached Jian'an, Shu abandoned the city and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Jian'an, Shu abandoned the city and fled south.

sentences.zh: 進次濁水，遣平西將軍楊靈珍擊文度所置仇池太守楊真，真眾潰，僅而得免。

translations.literal: Advancing to lodge at Zhuo River, he sent General Who Pacifies the West Yang Lingzhen to attack Yang Zhen, whom Wendu had installed as Administrator of Qiu Pool; Zhen's troops collapsed and he barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Zhuo River, he dispatched General Yang Lingzhen to attack Yang Zhen, Wendu's appointee as Administrator of Qiu Pool; Zhen's force was routed and he barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 喜遂軍於覆津。

translations.literal: Xi then encamped at Fu Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Xi then encamped at Fu Ford.

sentences.zh: 文度將強大黑固守津道，懸崖險絕，偏閣單行。

translations.literal: Wende's general Qiang Dahei held the ford road firm; cliff faces were perilously sheer, and only a narrow gallery allowed single-file passage.
translations.idiomatic: Wende's general Qiang Dahei held the ford road; the cliffs were sheer and perilous, passable only by a narrow catwalk.

sentences.zh: 喜部分將士，攀崖涉水，衝擊大黑，大黑潰走，追奔西入。

translations.literal: Xi divided officers and soldiers, scaled cliffs and crossed water, struck Dahei, Dahei's force collapsed and fled, and pursuit chased them westward.
translations.idiomatic: Xi divided his officers and men, scaled cliffs and crossed streams, and charged Dahei, who broke and fled; the pursuit drove them deep into the west.

sentences.zh: 攻葭蘆城，拔之，斬文度，傳首京師，殺一千餘人。

translations.literal: He attacked Jialu city, took it, beheaded Wendu, sent the head to the capital, and killed more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed Jialu, captured the city, beheaded Wendu, sent his head to the capital, and killed more than a thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夫忠臣生於德義之門，智勇出於將相之族。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Loyal ministers are born from gates of virtue and righteousness; wisdom and courage come from families of generals and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "True loyalty springs from households steeped in virtue; wisdom and valor come from lines of generals and ministers.

sentences.zh: 往年氐羌放命，侵竊邊戍，都將皮喜、梁醜奴等，或資父舊勳，或身建殊效，威名著於庸漢，公義列於天府，故授以節鉞，委閫外之任。

translations.literal: In former years the Di and Qiang cast off obedience and raided the frontier garrisons; commander Pi Xi, Liang Chounu, and others, some drawing on their fathers' old merit, some personally establishing special achievement—their martial fame noted in Yong and Han, their public righteousness enrolled in the Heavenly Repository—therefore the command tally and axe were conferred upon them and the charge outside the gate was entrusted to them.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the Di and Qiang had rebelled and raided the frontier; Commanders Pi Xi, Liang Chounu, and others—some inheriting their fathers' merit, some winning distinction with their own swords—their fame rang across Yong and Han and their loyalty was recorded in the imperial rolls; therefore they received imperial commissions and frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 並罄力盡銳，克荷所司，霜戈始動，蟻賊奔散，仇池旋復，民夷晏安。

translations.literal: All exhausted their strength and deployed their keenest blades, bearing well the duties entrusted; as frost-bright spears first moved, ant-like bandits scattered in flight; Qiu Pool was soon recovered and barbarians and people alike were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: They gave their full strength; as soon as their armies marched, the rebels scattered like ants; Qiu Pool was swiftly recovered and peace returned to Han and non-Han alike.

sentences.zh: 及討葭蘆，又梟凶醜。

translations.literal: When it came to chastising Jialu, they again displayed the heads of the wicked villains.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Jialu they again cut down the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 元惡俱殲，闚𨵦永息，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: The chief evildoers were all destroyed, covetous probing forever stilled—I greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: The arch-criminals were all destroyed and frontier raids ceased—I am deeply pleased.

sentences.zh: 其所陳計略，商校利害，料其應否，寧邊益國，專之可也。

translations.literal: The strategies they set forth, weighing benefit against harm and assessing what will or will not answer—whatever pacifies the frontier and benefits the state, let them decide exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: The plans they propose, weighing costs and benefits and judging what will work—whatever secures the border and strengthens the realm, they may decide on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 今軍威既振，羣愚懾服，革弊崇新，有易因之勢，寬猛之宜，任其量處，應立郡縣者，亦聽銓置。

translations.literal: Now that military prestige is already stirred and the masses of the foolish are awed into submission, to reform abuses and exalt the new there is an easy momentum to ride; as to what balance of lenience and severity suits, let them measure and dispose; where commanderies and counties ought to be established, permission is granted to assess and appoint.
translations.idiomatic: Now that our armies have prevailed and the people submit in awe, the moment favors reform; they may calibrate leniency and severity as they see fit, and where new commanderies and counties are needed, they may establish them as they judge appropriate.

sentences.zh: 其楊文度、楊鼠親屬家累，部送赴臺。

translations.literal: As for the kin and household dependents of Yang Wendu and Yang Shu, escort them and send them to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The families and dependents of Yang Wendu and Yang Shu are to be escorted to the capital.

sentences.zh: 仇池，南秦之根本，守禦資儲，特須豐積，險阻之要，尤宜守防，令奸覘之徒，絕其僥倖。

translations.literal: Qiu Pool is the root foundation of Southern Qin; defensive stores must especially be abundantly accumulated; strategic passes must above all be guarded and defended, so that spying villains may be cut off from their vain hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Pool is the foundation of Southern Qin; its stores of supplies must be fully stocked and its strategic passes strongly garrisoned, denying spies any chance of success.

sentences.zh: 勉勤戎務，綏靜新俗，懷民安土，稱朕意焉。」

translations.literal: Strive diligently in military affairs, pacify and settle new customs, cherish the people and secure the land—this accords with my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Devote yourselves to military duty, pacify the newly submitted peoples, comfort the people and secure the soil—this is what I expect of you."

sentences.zh: 又詔喜等曰：「卿受命專征，薄伐邊寇，軍威所及，即皆平蕩，復仇池之舊鎮，破葭蘆之新邦，梟擒首逆，克剪凶黨，勳庸之美，朕無間然。

translations.literal: Another edict addressed Xi and the others, saying, "You received the command for independent expedition, lightly chastised the frontier bandits; wherever military prestige reached, all was leveled and swept clean; the old garrison of Qiu Pool was recovered, the new stronghold of Jialu broken; ringleaders were beheaded and captured, villainous factions cut down—the beauty of your merit and service, I find no flaw in it.
translations.idiomatic: A further edict addressed Xi and his colleagues: "You were commissioned to campaign independently against the frontier raiders; wherever your armies went, the enemy was swept away; you restored Qiu Pool and destroyed Jialu, captured the rebel leaders and crushed their followers—your achievements leave nothing to be desired.

sentences.zh: 仇池國之要蕃，防守事宜，尤須完實。

translations.literal: Qiu Pool is a vital barrier of the state; matters of defense especially require thorough completion.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Pool is a vital frontier stronghold; its defenses must be made fully secure.

sentences.zh: 從前以來，駱谷置鎮，是以姦賊息闚𨵦之心，邊城無危敗之禍，近由徙就建安，致有往年之役。

translations.literal: From times past, establishing a garrison at Luogu Valley had caused villainous bandits to cease their covetous designs and frontier cities to be free from the calamity of perilous defeat; recently, because of relocation to Jian'an, there came last year's campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, a garrison at Luogu Valley kept enemy raiders from coveting our territory and frontier cities safe from disaster; but after it was moved to Jian'an, we suffered last year's campaign.

sentences.zh: 前敕卿等，部率兵將，駱谷築城，雖有一時之勤，終致永延之固。

translations.literal: Previously I charged you to lead troops and generals in building a city at Luogu Valley; though there would be labor for a time, in the end it would yield enduring solidity.
translations.idiomatic: I previously ordered you to lead your forces in building a fortress at Luogu Valley—a brief effort that would bring lasting security.

sentences.zh: 而卿等不祗詔命，至于今日，徒使兵人稽頓，無事閑停，方復曲辭，表求罷下，豈是良將忘身、憂國盡忠之謂也？

translations.literal: Yet you did not revere the edict's command, down to this day, vainly causing soldiers to linger stalled and idle without occupation, and now again with evasive words memorialize seeking to stop and withdraw—is this what is meant by a good general forgetting self and exhausting loyalty in concern for the state?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you disobeyed my order; your troops have been idle for months, and now you plead with evasions to be relieved—is this how a loyal general who puts his country first behaves?

sentences.zh: 諸州之兵，已復一歲，宜暫戮力，成此要功。

translations.literal: The troops of the various provinces have already been mustered for a full year; you should for the moment join forces and accomplish this vital work.
translations.idiomatic: Troops from the provinces have already been under arms for a year; you should combine your efforts and complete this essential fortification.

sentences.zh: 卿等表求來年築城，豈不更勞兵將？

translations.literal: You memorialize requesting to build the city next year—would that not further weary troops and generals?
translations.idiomatic: You ask to postpone construction until next year—would that not only burden the troops again?

sentences.zh: 孰若因今兵勢，即令就之，一勞永逸，事不再舉也。

translations.literal: How much better to rely on the present military momentum and have them proceed at once—one labor, enduring ease, the task not raised again.
translations.idiomatic: Better to use the forces already here and build now—one effort for lasting peace, rather than undertaking the work twice.

sentences.zh: 今更給軍糧一月，速於駱谷築城，使四月盡必令成就訖。

translations.literal: Now I further grant one month's army grain; speedily build the city at Luogu Valley, and by the end of the fourth month it must be brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: I am granting one more month's rations; build at Luogu Valley immediately and finish the fortress by the end of the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 若不時營築，乃築而不成，成而不固，以軍法從事。」

translations.literal: If you do not fortify in timely fashion, or build yet fail to complete, or complete yet fail to make firm, military law will be applied."
translations.idiomatic: Failure to build on schedule, or to build soundly and securely, will be punished under military law."

sentences.zh: 南天水郡民柳旃據險不順，喜率眾討滅之。

translations.literal: Liu Zhan, a commoner of Southern Tianshui Commandery, held perilous terrain in rebellion; Xi led troops to chastise and destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan, a native of Southern Tianshui Commandery, rebelled from mountainous strongholds; Xi led a force that crushed him.

sentences.zh: 轉散騎常侍、安南將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Imperial Escort, General Who Pacifies the South, and Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the South, and Inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 詔讓其在州寬怠，以飲酒廢事，威不禁下，遣使者就州決以杖罰。

translations.literal: An edict reproached him for laxness and neglect in the province, for abandoning duties through drink, and for authority that did not restrain subordinates; an envoy was sent to the province to decide on beating with the staff as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The court reprimanded him for lax governance, neglect of duty through drunkenness, and failure to maintain discipline; an envoy was sent to Yu Province to administer corporal punishment.

sentences.zh: 七年卒，贈以本官，諡曰恭公。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died; his former office was posthumously granted, with the posthumous title Duke Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year; his final rank was conferred posthumously, with the posthumous name Duke Gong.

sentences.zh: 子承宗襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Chengzong inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengzong succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 喜弟雙仁，冠軍將軍、仇池鎮將。

translations.literal: Xi's younger brother Shuangren was General Who Establishes Champions and Commander of Qiu Pool Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's younger brother Shuangren served as General Who Establishes Champions and garrison commander of Qiu Pool.

sentences.zh: 封敕文，代人也。

translations.literal: Feng Chiwen was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Chiwen was a native of Dai.

sentences.zh: 祖豆，皇始初領眾三萬東征幽州，平定三郡，拜幽州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dou, at the beginning of Huangshi, led thirty thousand men east to campaign against You Province, pacified three commanderies, and was appointed Inspector of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dou, at the start of Huangshi, led thirty thousand men on an eastern campaign into You Province, pacified three commanderies, and was appointed Inspector of You Province.

sentences.zh: 後為使持節、都督冀青二州諸軍事、前將軍、開府、冀青二州刺史、關內侯。

translations.literal: Later he served as Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the Two Provinces of Ji and Qing, Forward General, with headquarters established, Inspector of the Two Provinces of Ji and Qing, and Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in Ji and Qing, Forward General with headquarters, Inspector of Ji and Qing, and Marquis within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 父涅，太宗時為侍御長。

translations.literal: His father Nie, in the time of Emperor Daozong, served as Chief Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Nie served as Chief Palace Attendant under Emperor Daozong.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈龍驤將軍、定州刺史、章武侯，諡曰隱。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously granted Dragon-Courser General, Inspector of Ding Province, and Marquis of Zhangwu, with the posthumous title Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his death he was posthumously honored as Dragon-Courser General, Inspector of Ding Province, and Marquis of Zhangwu, with the posthumous name Yin.

sentences.zh: 敕文，始光初為中散，稍遷西部尚書。

translations.literal: Chiwen, at the beginning of Shiguang, served as Palace Attendant and gradually was promoted to Minister of the Western Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwen entered service as a palace attendant at the start of Shiguang and was gradually promoted to Minister of the Western Bureau.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節、散騎常侍、鎮西將軍、開府、領護西夷校尉、秦益二州刺史，賜爵天水公，鎮上邽。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Imperial Escort, General Who Guards the West, with headquarters established, concurrently Colonel Protector of the Western Yi, Inspector of the Two Provinces of Qin and Yi, enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui, garrisoning Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched as Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, General Who Guards the West with headquarters, Colonel Protector of the Western Yi, and Inspector of Qin and Yi, ennobled as Duke of Tianshui and stationed at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 詔敕文率步騎七千征吐谷渾慕利延兄子拾歸於枹罕，眾少不能制，詔遣安遠將軍、廣川公乙烏頭等二軍與敕文會隴右。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chiwen to lead seven thousand infantry and cavalry to campaign against Muli Yan's nephew Shigui of Tuyuhun at Fuhan; his force was too few to control him, so an edict dispatched two armies under General Who Pacifies the Distant, Duke of Guangchuan Yi Wutou, and others to join Chiwen in Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Chiwen to lead seven thousand infantry and cavalry against Shigui, nephew of the Tuyuhun leader Muli Yan, at Fuhan; his force was too small to contain the enemy, so two armies under General Yi Wutou, Duke of Guangchuan, were sent to join him in Longyou.

sentences.zh: 軍次武始，拾歸夜遁。

translations.literal: The army halted at Wushi; Shigui fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Wushi; Shigui fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 敕文引軍入枹罕，虜拾歸妻子及其民戶，分徙千家於上邽，留烏頭守枹罕。

translations.literal: Chiwen led his army into Fuhan, captured Shigui's wife and children together with his households, resettled a thousand families at Shanggui, and left Wutou to guard Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwen marched into Fuhan, seized Shigui's family and followers, resettled a thousand households at Shanggui, and left Wutou to garrison Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 金城邊冏、天水梁會謀反，扇動秦益二州雜人萬餘戶，據上邽東城。

translations.literal: Bian Jiong of Jincheng and Liang Hui of Tianshui plotted rebellion, inciting more than ten thousand households of mixed populations in the Two Provinces of Qin and Yi, and seized the eastern city of Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Jiong of Jincheng and Liang Hui of Tianshui plotted rebellion, stirring more than ten thousand households of various peoples in Qin and Yi to rise up and seize the eastern quarter of Shanggui.

sentences.zh: [6]攻逼西城。

translations.literal: [6] They attacked and pressed the western city.
translations.idiomatic: [6] They then assaulted the western quarter of the city.

sentences.zh: 敕文先已設備，殺賊百餘人，被傷者眾，賊乃引退。

translations.literal: Chiwen had already made preparations; more than a hundred rebels were killed, many were wounded, and the bandits then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwen had already prepared defenses; more than a hundred rebels were killed and many wounded, and the attackers withdrew.

sentences.zh: 冏、會復率眾四千攻城，氐羌一萬屯於南嶺，休官、屠各及諸雜戶二萬餘人屯於北嶺，為冏等形援。

translations.literal: Jiong and Hui again led four thousand men to attack the city; ten thousand Di and Qiang encamped on the southern ridge; more than twenty thousand Xiu'guan, Tuge, and various other mixed households encamped on the northern ridge, serving as visible support for Jiong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong and Hui returned with four thousand men to attack the city; ten thousand Di and Qiang camped on the southern ridge while more than twenty thousand Xiu'guan, Tuge, and other non-Han peoples camped on the northern ridge to support them.

sentences.zh: 敕文遣二將領騎二百設備門內，別令騎出擊之。

translations.literal: Chiwen sent two generals leading two hundred cavalry to take position inside the gate, and separately ordered cavalry out to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwen posted two generals with two hundred cavalry inside the gates and sent other horsemen out to attack.

sentences.zh: 既而偽退，冏率眾騰逐，敕文輕騎橫衝，大破之，斬冏。

translations.literal: Then feigning retreat, as Jiong led his masses in leaping pursuit, Chiwen's light cavalry struck crosswise, inflicting a great defeat and beheading Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwen's cavalry feigned retreat; as Jiong gave chase, Chiwen's light horsemen wheeled and charged, winning a crushing victory and killing Jiong.

sentences.zh: 而北嶺之賊，從高射敕文軍人，飛矢如雨，梁會得奔北嶺，騎乃引還。

translations.literal: But the bandits on the northern ridge shot at Chiwen's soldiers from the heights; arrows flew like rain; Liang Hui was able to flee to the northern ridge, and the cavalry then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels on the northern ridge rained arrows down on Chiwen's troops; Liang Hui escaped to the north ridge, and the cavalry pulled back.

sentences.zh: 復推會為主。

translations.literal: They again proclaimed Hui as leader.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then rallied behind Hui as their leader.

sentences.zh: 敕文分兵二百人突入南城，燒其門樓，賊見火起，眾皆驚亂。

translations.literal: Chiwen divided two hundred men to burst into the southern city, burning its gate tower; seeing fire rise, the bandits were all alarmed and thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwen sent two hundred men into the southern city, set fire to the gate tower, and the rebels panicked at the blaze.

sentences.zh: 又遣步卒攻門，克之，便率騎士馳入，賊餘眾開門出走，奔入東城，乘背追擊，殺千餘人。

translations.literal: He again sent foot soldiers to attack the gate and took it; then immediately leading horsemen he galloped in; the remaining bandits opened the gates and fled out, running into the eastern city; riding their backs he pursued and killed more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He sent infantry to storm the gate and break through, then charged in with cavalry; the surviving rebels fled through the gates into the eastern city, and pursuit from behind killed more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 安豐公閭根率軍助敕文。

translations.literal: Lu Gen, Duke of Anfeng, led an army to assist Chiwen.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gen, Duke of Anfeng, marched with reinforcements to aid Chiwen.

sentences.zh: 敕文表曰：「安定逆賊帥路那羅遣使齎書與逆帥梁會，會以那羅書射於城中，那羅稱纂集眾旅，剋期助會。

translations.literal: Chiwen memorialized, saying, "Lu Naruo, rebel chieftain of Anding, sent an envoy bearing a letter to the rebel chieftain Liang Hui; Hui shot Naruo's letter into the city. Naruo declared he was gathering masses of troops and would join Hui on a set day.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwen submitted a memorial: "Lu Naruo, rebel leader of Anding, sent a messenger with a letter to Liang Hui; Hui had the letter shot into the city. Naruo claimed he was gathering troops and would arrive on a set date to assist Hui.

sentences.zh: 又仇池城民李洪，自稱應王，天授玉璽，擅作符書，誑惑百姓。

translations.literal: Moreover, Li Hong, a commoner of Qiu Pool city, proclaimed himself the Responsive King, claiming heaven had bestowed the jade seal; he presumptuously forged talismanic writs and deceived the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hong, a man of Qiu Pool city, also proclaimed himself the Responsive King, claiming a jade seal conferred by heaven; he forged prophetic documents and misled the populace.

sentences.zh: 梁會遣使招引楊文德，而文德遣權壽胡將兵二十人來到會間，扇動州土，云李洪自稱應王，兩雄不並，若欲須我，先殺李洪，我當自往。

translations.literal: Liang Hui sent an envoy to summon Yang Wende; Wende dispatched Quan Shouhu leading twenty men to come among Hui's forces, inciting the province, saying, "Li Hong has proclaimed himself Responsive King; two heroes cannot stand together—if you want me, kill Li Hong first and I will come myself."
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hui sent envoys to enlist Yang Wende; Wende dispatched Quan Shouhu with twenty soldiers to Hui's camp, stirring up the region with the message: "Li Hong has declared himself king—two powers cannot coexist; if you want my help, kill Li Hong first and I will come in person."

sentences.zh: 梁會欲引致文德，誘說李洪來入東城，即斬洪首，送與文德。

translations.literal: Liang Hui wished to draw Wende in; he enticed and persuaded Li Hong to enter the eastern city, then immediately beheaded Hong and sent the head to Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to win Wende's alliance, Hui lured Li Hong into the eastern city, then beheaded him and sent his head to Wende.

sentences.zh: 仇池鎮將、淮陽公臣豹子遣使潛行，以今月二十四日來達臣鎮，稱楊文德受劉義隆職爵，領兵聚眾，在仇池境中，沮動民人，規竊城鎮。

translations.literal: The Commander of Qiu Pool Garrison, Lord Baozi, Duke of Huaiyang, sent an envoy by secret route; on the twenty-fourth of this month he reached my garrison, reporting that Yang Wende had received office and title from Liu Yilong, was gathering troops and mustering followers within Qiu Pool's borders, discouraging and inciting the people, and scheming to seize cities and garrison posts.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi, Duke of Huaiyang and garrison commander of Qiu Pool, sent a secret messenger who reached my post on the twenty-fourth of this month, reporting that Yang Wende had accepted rank from Liu Yilong, was raising troops within Qiu Pool territory, stirring up the people, and plotting to seize our posts.

sentences.zh: 且梁會反逆以來，南勾文德，援勢相連，武都氐羌盡相脣齒，為文德起軍，所在屯結，兵眾已集，剋來不遠。

translations.literal: Moreover, since Liang Hui's rebellion, he has connived southward with Wende and their supportive power links together; the Di and Qiang of Wudu all act as lip and teeth; armies have been raised for Wende, encamping and gathering everywhere—the troops are already assembled and the day of attack is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liang Hui's revolt he has been in league with Wende to the south; the Di and Qiang of Wudu stand together like lips and teeth; forces rallying to Wende are encamped throughout the region—their attack will come soon.

sentences.zh: 臣備邊鎮，與賊相持，賊在東城，隔牆而已。

translations.literal: I garrison the frontier post, locked in stalemate with the bandits; the bandits are in the eastern city, separated from me by only a wall.
translations.idiomatic: I hold the frontier garrison locked in stalemate with the rebels—they occupy the eastern city, just a wall away.

sentences.zh: 但以腹背有敵，攻城有疑，討度文德，[7]剋來助會。

translations.literal: But with enemies front and rear, and doubts about storming the city, considering Wende, [7] he will surely come to aid Hui on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Yet with foes at my front and rear and the siege still uncertain, I reckon Wende [7] will arrive on schedule to reinforce Hui.

sentences.zh: 若文德既至，百姓響應，賊黨遂甚，用功益難。

translations.literal: If Wende has already arrived and the common people respond, the rebel faction will grow stronger and the effort will become harder still.
translations.idiomatic: If Wende arrives and the people rally to him, the rebels will grow stronger and victory will become far harder.

sentences.zh: 今文德未到，麥復未熟，事宜速擊，於時為便。

translations.literal: Now Wende has not yet arrived and the wheat is again not ripe—the affair calls for a swift strike; the time is opportune.
translations.idiomatic: Wende has not yet come, and the wheat is still unripe—this is the moment to strike swiftly, while conditions favor us.

sentences.zh: 伏願天鑒，時遣大軍，助臣誅翦。」

translations.literal: I humbly pray Heaven's discernment to dispatch a great army in good time to help your servant exterminate and cut them down."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to see clearly and send a great army in time to help me destroy them."

sentences.zh: 表未及報，梁會謀欲逃遁。

translations.literal: Before the memorial could receive a reply, Liang Hui plotted to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Before the memorial received a response, Liang Hui plotted escape.

sentences.zh: 先是，敕文掘重壍於東城之外，斷賊走路。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chiwen had dug a deep trench outside the eastern city to cut off the bandits' route of flight.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chiwen had dug a deep trench outside the eastern city to block the rebels' escape route.

sentences.zh: 夜中，會乃車陳飛梯，騰壍而走。

translations.literal: In the middle of the night, Hui then arrayed chariots and scaling ladders, leaped the trench, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the dead of night Hui deployed chariots and scaling ladders, vaulted the trench, and fled.

sentences.zh: 敕文先嚴兵於壍外拒鬬，從夜至旦。

translations.literal: Chiwen had first posted troops in strength outside the trench to resist battle, from night until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwen had already massed troops outside the trench to meet them in battle, fighting from night until dawn.

sentences.zh: 敕文謀於眾曰：「困獸猶鬬，而況於人。

translations.literal: Chiwen consulted the assembly, saying, "A cornered beast still fights—how much more so men.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwen consulted his officers, saying, "Even a cornered beast will fight—how much more so men.

sentences.zh: 賊眾知無生路，人自致死，必傷士眾，未易可平。

translations.literal: The rebel masses, knowing there is no way to live, will each fight to the death; they will surely wound our soldiers and troops, and will not be easily pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing they have no way out, the rebels will fight to the death, inflicting heavy casualties on our men—they will not be easily subdued.

sentences.zh: 若開其生路，賊必上下離心，克之易矣。」

translations.literal: If we open a way for them to live, the bandits above and below will surely lose heart, and taking them will be easy."
translations.idiomatic: If we leave them a path to survival, the rebels will lose heart from top to bottom, and victory will come easily."

sentences.zh: 眾咸以為然。

translations.literal: All agreed this was so.
translations.idiomatic: All present agreed.

sentences.zh: 初敕文以白虎幡宣告賊眾曰：「若能歸降，原其生命。」

translations.literal: At first Chiwen, with a white-tiger banner, proclaimed to the rebel masses, saying, "If you can surrender, I will spare your lives."
translations.idiomatic: Chiwen first raised a white-tiger banner and proclaimed to the rebels: "Surrender, and your lives will be spared."

sentences.zh: 應時降者六百餘人。

translations.literal: More than six hundred surrendered on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: More than six hundred surrendered at once.

sentences.zh: 會知人心沮壞，於是分遁。

translations.literal: Hui, knowing men's hearts were broken and demoralized, thereupon dispersed and fled in separate groups.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing morale collapse, Hui broke his forces into groups and fled.

sentences.zh: 敕文縱騎躡之，死者太半，俘獲四千五百餘口。
