translations.literal: Chiwen released cavalry to pursue them; more than half died, and more than four thousand five hundred persons were captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwen sent cavalry in pursuit; more than half were killed, and over forty-five hundred were taken alive.

sentences.zh: 長子萬護，讓爵於弟翰。

translations.literal: His eldest son Wanhu ceded the title to his younger brother Han.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Wanhu yielded the title to his younger brother Han.

sentences.zh: 於時讓者惟萬護及元氏侯趙辟惡子元伯讓其弟次興，朝廷義而許之。

translations.literal: At that time those who yielded titles were only Wanhu and Yuan Bo, son of Marquis Zhao Bie of the Yuan clan, who yielded to his younger brother Ci Xing; the court honored their righteousness and granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: At the time only Wanhu and Yuan Bo, son of Marquis Zhao Bie of the Yuan clan—who yielded to his younger brother Ci Xing—voluntarily surrendered their titles; the court admired their virtue and approved.

sentences.zh: 翰族孫靜，世宗時，歷位征虜將軍、武衞將軍、太子左衞率，以幹用稱。

translations.literal: Jing, a clansman-grandson of Han's line, in the time of Emperor Xuanwu successively held the posts of General Who Subdues Barbarians, General of the Martial Guard, and Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, and was known for competence and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, a clansman of Han's line, served under Emperor Xuanwu as General Who Subdues Barbarians, General of the Martial Guard, and Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, earning renown for his competence.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，遷平北將軍、恒州刺史，臨朐子。

translations.literal: In the Yanchang era he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Heng province, with the title Marquis of Linqu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanchang era he was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Heng province, enfeoffed as Marquis of Linqu.

sentences.zh: 後坐事免。

translations.literal: Later, because of an offense he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was later dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子熙，奉朝請。

translations.literal: His son Xi served as Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi served as Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 遷員外散騎侍郎、給事中，與薛曇尚迎蠕蠕主婆羅門於涼州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Extra Master of Writing and Attendant Gentleman, and together with Xue Tanshang received the Rouran ruler Poluomen at Liang province.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Extra Master of Writing and Attendant Gentleman, and with Xue Tanshang escorted the Rouran ruler Poluomen to Liang province.

sentences.zh: 又除鎮遠將軍、河陰令。

translations.literal: He was again appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant and Magistrate of Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant and Magistrate of Heyin.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈輔國將軍、朔州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was granted General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Shuo province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Shuo province.

sentences.zh: 子纘，武定末，潁川太守。

translations.literal: His son Zuan, at the end of the Wuding era, served as Administrator of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuan served as Administrator of Yingchuan in the late Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 呂羅漢，本東平壽張人。

translations.literal: Lu Luohan was originally a man of Shouzhang in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Luohan was a native of Shouzhang in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 其先，石勒時徙居幽州。

translations.literal: His ancestors, in the time of Shi Le, were relocated to You province.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had been relocated to You province during the reign of Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 祖顯，字子明。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xian, courtesy name Ziming.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xian, courtesy name Ziming.

sentences.zh: 少好學，性廉直，鄉人有分爭者皆就而質焉。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning; his nature was upright and honest; when fellow townsmen had disputes they all came to him for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and was upright by nature; neighbors in dispute came to him for judgment.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂以為河間太守。

translations.literal: Murong Chui appointed him Administrator of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui appointed him Administrator of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 皇始初，以郡來降，太祖嘉之，賜爵魏昌男，拜鉅鹿太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangshi, he surrendered the commandery and came over; Emperor Taizu commended him, bestowed the title Baron of Weichang, and appointed him Administrator of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Huangshi era he surrendered his commandery to Wei; Emperor Taizu praised him, enfeoffed him as Baron of Weichang, and made him Administrator of Julu.

sentences.zh: 清身奉公，務存贍卹，妻子不免飢寒。

translations.literal: He kept himself pure and served the public, striving to provide relief and support; his wife and children could not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: He lived simply and served the public faithfully, devoting himself to relief work—yet his wife and children still knew hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 民頌之曰：「時惟府君，克己清明。

translations.literal: The people praised him in song, saying, "At this time our magistrate restrains himself and is clear and bright.
translations.idiomatic: The people sang his praise: "In this age our magistrate is self-restrained and incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 緝我荒土，民胥樂生。

translations.literal: He brings order to our wasted land; the people all rejoice in life.
translations.idiomatic: He has restored our wasted lands; all the people rejoice in life.

sentences.zh: 願壽無疆，以享長齡。」

translations.literal: May his years be without limit, that he may enjoy long life."
translations.idiomatic: May he live without end and enjoy long years."

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 父溫，字晞陽。

translations.literal: His father Wen, courtesy name Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wen, courtesy name Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 善書，好施，有文武才略。

translations.literal: He was skilled at calligraphy, fond of generosity, and possessed both civil and military talent and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He was an accomplished calligrapher, generous by nature, and gifted in both civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 世祖伐赫連昌，以溫為幢將。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu campaigned against Helian Chang, Wen served as standard-bearer general.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu marched against Helian Chang, Wen served as standard-bearer general.

sentences.zh: 先登陷陳，每戰必捷，以功拜宣威將軍、奉車都尉。

translations.literal: He was first to ascend and break the enemy line; in every battle he was victorious; for his merit he was appointed General Who Proclaims Might and Bearer of the Imperial Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He led the charge in every assault and won every battle; for his merit he was made General Who Proclaims Might and Bearer of the Imperial Carriage.

sentences.zh: 出為秦州司馬，遷上黨太守，善勸課，有治名。

translations.literal: He went out as Qin province Vice-Governor, was transferred to Administrator of Shangdang, and was skilled at encouraging agriculture and taxation, with a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice-Governor of Qin province, then as Administrator of Shangdang, where his skill at promoting agriculture earned him a reputation for effective rule.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平遠將軍、豫州刺史、野王侯，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was granted General Who Pacifies the Distant, Inspector of Yu province, and Marquis of Yewang, with the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Distant, Inspector of Yu province, and Marquis of Yewang, with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 羅漢仁篤慎密，弱冠以武幹知名。

translations.literal: Luohan was benevolent, sincere, and careful; from youth he was known for martial ability.
translations.idiomatic: Luohan was steadfast, sincere, and meticulous; from youth he was known for his martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 父溫之佐秦州，羅漢隨侍。

translations.literal: When his father Wen served as assistant in Qin province, Luohan followed and attended him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Wen served in Qin province, Luohan accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 隴右氐楊難當率眾數萬寇上邽，秦民多應之。

translations.literal: Yang Nandang of the Di in Longyou led several tens of thousands in raiding Shanggui, and many Qin commoners responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nandang of the Longyou Di led tens of thousands against Shanggui, and many people of Qin rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 鎮將元意頭知羅漢善射，共登西城樓，令羅漢射難當隊將及兵二十三人，應弦而殪。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Yuan Yitou, knowing Luohan was skilled at archery, together ascended the western city tower and had Luohan shoot at Nandang's squad leaders and soldiers—twenty-three men in all—and they fell at the twang of the bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Yuan Yitou, knowing Luohan's skill with the bow, joined him on the western tower and had him shoot Nandang's squad leaders and soldiers—twenty-three men in all—each falling at the twang of the string.

sentences.zh: 賊眾轉盛，羅漢進計曰：「今若不出戰，示敵以弱，眾情攜貳，大事去矣。」

translations.literal: The rebel masses grew stronger still; Luohan advanced a plan, saying, "If we do not go out to battle now, showing the enemy weakness, the people's hearts will waver and split—the great affair will be lost."
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels grew stronger, Luohan proposed: "If we refuse battle now and show weakness, morale will fracture and all will be lost."

sentences.zh: 意頭善之，即簡千餘騎令羅漢出戰。

translations.literal: Yitou approved this and immediately selected more than a thousand cavalry and ordered Luohan out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yitou agreed and immediately selected more than a thousand horsemen and sent Luohan out to fight.

sentences.zh: 羅漢與諸騎策馬大呼，直衝難當軍，眾皆披靡。

translations.literal: Luohan, with the other horsemen, spurred their horses and shouted loudly, charging straight into Nandang's army; the masses all scattered and fell back.
translations.idiomatic: Luohan and his riders spurred their horses forward with a great shout and charged straight into Nandang's army, which broke and scattered.

sentences.zh: 殺難當左右隊騎八人，難當大驚。

translations.literal: They killed eight of the horsemen of Nandang's left and right squads; Nandang was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: They killed eight of Nandang's escort riders, and Nandang was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 會世祖賜難當璽書，責其跋扈，難當乃引還仇池。

translations.literal: Just then Emperor Taiwu sent Nandang an imperial letter under seal reproaching his arrogance and insubordination; Nandang thereupon led his forces back to Chou Pool.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Emperor Taiwu sent Nandang an imperial letter under seal rebuking his arrogance, and Nandang withdrew to Chou Pool.

sentences.zh: 意頭具以狀聞，世祖嘉之，徵為羽林中郎。

translations.literal: Yitou fully reported the circumstances; Emperor Taiwu commended him and summoned Luohan as Palace Guard Central Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Yitou reported the full account; Emperor Taiwu praised Luohan and summoned him to serve as Palace Guard Central Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 上邽休官呂豐、屠各王飛廉等八千餘家，[8]據險為逆，詔羅漢率騎一千討擒之。

translations.literal: More than eight thousand households of Lu Feng, a retired official of Shanggui, and Wang Feilian of the Tuge, [8] held perilous ground in rebellion; an edict ordered Luohan to lead a thousand cavalry to campaign against and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Feng, a retired official of Shanggui, and Wang Feilian of the Tuge, with more than eight thousand households, [8] held rugged terrain in rebellion; Luohan was ordered to lead a thousand cavalry to suppress and capture them.

sentences.zh: 從征懸瓠，羅漢與琅邪王司馬楚之駕前招慰，降者九千餘戶。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Xuanchi, Luohan together with the Prince of Langye's Staff Major Chu Zhi rode ahead to summon and reassure; more than nine thousand households surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On the Xuanchi campaign Luohan rode ahead with Chu Zhi, Staff Major to the Prince of Langye, to offer terms; more than nine thousand households surrendered.

sentences.zh: 比至盱眙，頻破賊軍，擒其將顧儼、李觀之等。

translations.literal: By the time they reached Xuyi, they repeatedly broke the rebel armies and captured their generals Gu Yan and Li Guanzhi and others.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached Xuyi they had repeatedly defeated rebel forces and captured the generals Gu Yan, Li Guanzhi, and others.

sentences.zh: 以功遷羽林中郎、幢將，賜爵烏程子，加建威將軍。

translations.literal: For his merit he was transferred to Palace Guard Central Gentleman and standard-bearer general, was bestowed the title Viscount of Wucheng, and was given additionally the rank of General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made Palace Guard Central Gentleman and standard-bearer general, enfeoffed as Viscount of Wucheng, and given the additional rank of General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 及南安王余立，羅漢猶典宿衞，高宗之立，羅漢有力焉。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Nan'an, Yu, was installed, Luohan still supervised the palace guard; when Emperor Wencheng was installed, Luohan had a strong hand in it.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu of Nan'an was placed on the throne, Luohan still commanded the palace guard; he also played a decisive role in Emperor Wencheng's accession.

sentences.zh: 遷少卿，仍幢將，進爵野王侯，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Junior Chamberlain, still standard-bearer general; he advanced in title to Marquis of Yewang and was given additionally the rank of General of the Flying Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Junior Chamberlain while retaining his post as standard-bearer general, promoted to Marquis of Yewang, and given the additional rank of General of the Flying Dragon.

sentences.zh: 拜司衞監，遷散騎常侍、殿中尚書，進爵山陽公，加鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervisor of the Palace Guard, transferred to Regular Attendant and Palace Secretary, advanced in title to Duke of Shanyang, and given additionally the rank of General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Supervisor of the Palace Guard, then Regular Attendant and Palace Secretary, promoted to Duke of Shanyang, and given the additional rank of General Who Guards the West.

sentences.zh: 及蠕蠕犯塞，顯祖討之，羅漢與右僕射南平公元目振都督中外軍事。

translations.literal: When the Rouran violated the frontier, Emperor Xiaowen campaigned against them; Luohan together with Right Vice Director Yuan Muzhen of Nanping jointly supervised military affairs at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran raided the frontier, Emperor Xiaowen marched against them; Luohan and Right Vice Director Yuan Muzhen of Nanping jointly commanded all military affairs.

sentences.zh: 出為鎮西將軍、秦益二州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Guards the West and Inspector of the Two Provinces of Qin and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Qin and Yi provinces.

sentences.zh: 時仇池氐羌反，攻逼駱谷，鎮將吳保元走登百頃，請援於羅漢。

translations.literal: At that time the Di and Qiang of Chou Pool rebelled, attacking and pressing Luogu; the garrison commander Wu Baoyuan fled and climbed Baiqing, requesting aid from Luohan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Di and Qiang of Chou Pool rebelled and pressed Luogu; garrison commander Wu Baoyuan retreated to Baiqing and appealed to Luohan for relief.

sentences.zh: 羅漢帥步騎隨長孫觀掩擊氐羌，大破之，斬其渠帥，賊眾退散。

translations.literal: Luohan led infantry and cavalry following Zhangsun Guan in a surprise attack on the Di and Qiang, inflicting a great defeat, beheading their chieftains; the rebel masses dispersed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Luohan led infantry and cavalry with Zhangsun Guan in a surprise attack that routed the Di and Qiang, beheaded their chieftains, and scattered the rebels.

sentences.zh: 詔羅漢曰：「卿以勞勤獲敍，才能致用，內總禁旅，外臨方岳，褒寵之隆，可謂備矣。

translations.literal: An edict to Luohan said, "You, through labor and diligence, have earned advancement, and through talent have been put to use; within you command the forbidden guard, without you oversee a frontier province—the height of favor and honor may be called complete.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to Luohan read: "Through loyal service you have risen in rank, and through ability you have been entrusted with command—within, you lead the palace guard; without, you govern a frontier province. No honor could be greater.

sentences.zh: 自非盡節竭誠，將何以垂名竹帛？

translations.literal: If you do not exhaust your loyalty and pour out your sincerity, how will you leave your name on bamboo and silk?
translations.idiomatic: Unless you give your utmost loyalty and devotion, how will your name endure in the histories?

sentences.zh: 仇池接近邊境，兵革屢興，既勞士卒，亦動民庶，皆由鎮將不明，綏禁不理之所致也。

translations.literal: Chou Pool lies close to the frontier; arms and armor have repeatedly been raised; it has both wearied the soldiers and stirred the common people—all caused by garrison commanders who are not clear-sighted and who fail to govern pacification and prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Chou Pool lies on the frontier, where war has flared again and again, exhausting soldiers and unsettling the people—all because garrison commanders have been incompetent and failed to maintain order.

sentences.zh: 卿應機赴擊，殄此兇醜。

translations.literal: You responded to the moment and went to strike, exterminating these vicious villains.
translations.idiomatic: You acted at once and crushed these villains.

sentences.zh: 隴右土險，民亦剛悍，若不導之以德，齊之以刑，寇賊莫由可息，百姓無以得靜。

translations.literal: Longyou's terrain is rugged and its people are also fierce and stubborn; if you do not guide them with virtue and align them with punishment, bandits and rebels cannot be stilled, and the common people cannot obtain peace.
translations.idiomatic: Longyou is rugged country, its people fierce and stubborn; unless they are led by virtue and restrained by law, banditry will never cease and the people will never know peace.

sentences.zh: 朕垂心治道，欲使遠近清穆，卿可召集豪右，擇其事宜，以利民為先，益國為本，隨其風俗，以施威惠。

translations.literal: I bend my heart to the way of governance, wishing to make far and near clear and tranquil; you may summon the powerful and prominent, choose what fits the circumstances, take benefiting the people as foremost and enriching the state as foundation, and according to local custom apply authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: My heart is set on good governance and peace throughout the realm. Summon the local leaders, choose measures suited to conditions, put the people's welfare first and the state's strength as your foundation, and govern with both firmness and mercy according to local custom.

sentences.zh: 其有安土樂業、奉公勤私者，善加勸督，無奪時利。

translations.literal: Those who settle on the land and rejoice in their work, serving the public diligently in private affairs—kindly encourage and supervise them, and do not seize their seasonal profits.
translations.idiomatic: Encourage those who work the land in peace and serve the public faithfully, and do not deprive them of their seasonal gains.

sentences.zh: 明相宣告，稱朕意焉。」

translations.literal: Clearly proclaim this on my behalf, declaring my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim this clearly throughout the region on my behalf."

sentences.zh: 涇州民張羌郎扇惑隴東，聚眾千餘人，州軍討之不能制。

translations.literal: Zhang Qianglang of Jing province incited Longdong, gathering more than a thousand men; the provincial army campaigned against him but could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qianglang of Jing province stirred up Longdong, gathering more than a thousand followers; the provincial army could not suppress him.

sentences.zh: 羅漢率步騎一千擊羌郎，擒之。

translations.literal: Luohan led a thousand infantry and cavalry to strike Qianglang and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Luohan led a thousand infantry and cavalry against Qianglang and captured him.

sentences.zh: 仇池氐羌叛逆遂甚，所在蜂起，道路斷絕。

translations.literal: The Di and Qiang rebellion of Chou Pool grew severe; everywhere they swarmed up like bees; roads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The Di and Qiang rebellion at Chou Pool intensified; uprisings flared everywhere and roads were severed.

sentences.zh: 其賊帥蛩廉、符祈等皆受劉昱官爵、鐵券。

translations.literal: Their rebel chieftains Qiong Lian, Fu Qi, and others all received office, titles, and iron certificates from Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leaders Qiong Lian, Fu Qi, and others all received offices, titles, and iron certificates of investiture from Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 略陽公伏阿奴為都將，與羅漢赴討，所在破之，生擒廉、祈等。

translations.literal: Fu Anu, Duke of Lueyang, served as commander-in-chief and together with Luohan went to campaign; wherever they went they broke the enemy, capturing Lian, Qi, and others alive.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Anu, Duke of Lueyang, served as commander-in-chief and joined Luohan in the campaign; they defeated the rebels wherever they met them and took Lian, Qi, and others alive.

sentences.zh: 秦益阻遠，南連仇池，西接赤水，諸羌恃險，數為叛逆。

translations.literal: Qin and Yi were blocked and distant, connecting south with Chou Pool and west with Chishui; the various Qiang relied on perilous terrain and repeatedly rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Yi were remote provinces, bordering Chou Pool to the south and Chishui to the west; the Qiang peoples, sheltered by rugged terrain, rebelled again and again.

sentences.zh: 自羅漢莅州，撫以威惠，西戎懷德，土境帖然。

translations.literal: From the time Luohan arrived to govern the province, he soothed them with authority and kindness; the western barbarians cherished virtue, and the territory within the borders was calm and settled.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Luohan took office he governed with a balance of force and mercy; the western tribes submitted willingly, and the frontier lay quiet.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔羅漢曰：「朕總攝萬幾，統臨四海，思隆古道，光顯風教，故內委羣司，外任方牧，正是志士建節之秋，忠臣立功之會。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict Luohan, saying, "I overall grasp the myriad affairs and universally oversee the four seas, thinking to elevate the ancient way and brightly display customs and teaching; therefore within I entrust the various offices, without I appoint frontier governors—this is precisely the season for men of resolve to establish integrity, and the occasion for loyal ministers to establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen wrote to Luohan: "I oversee the myriad affairs of state and rule the four seas, seeking to revive the ways of antiquity and uphold moral teaching. Within I rely on my ministers; without I entrust frontier governors—this is the hour for men of principle to prove their loyalty and for faithful servants to earn lasting merit.

sentences.zh: 然赤水羌民，遠居邊土，非卿善誘，何以招輯？

translations.literal: Yet the Qiang people of Chishui dwell far on the frontier soil; unless you skillfully win them, how can they be summoned and gathered?
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang of Chishui live far on the frontier; without your skill in winning them over, how could they be brought to submit?

sentences.zh: 卿所得口馬，表求貢奉，朕嘉乃誠，便敕領納。

translations.literal: The captives and horses you obtained you memorialized requesting to present in tribute; I commend your sincerity and have ordered them received.
translations.idiomatic: You memorialized offering the captives and horses you had taken as tribute; I admire your loyalty and have ordered them accepted.

sentences.zh: 其馬印付都牧，口以賜卿。」

translations.literal: The horses' brands shall be delivered to the Directorate of Herds; the captives are bestowed upon you."
translations.idiomatic: The horses shall be sent to the imperial stud; the captives I grant to you."

sentences.zh: 徵拜內都大官，聽訟察獄，多得其情。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Grand Director of the Inner Palace, hearing lawsuits and examining prisons; in many cases he got to the truth of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Grand Director of the Inner Palace; in hearing cases and examining prisons he often reached the truth.

sentences.zh: 太和六年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taihe he died in office.

sentences.zh: 高祖深悼惜之，賜命服一襲，贈以本官，諡曰莊公。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen deeply mourned and regretted his loss, bestowed one set of court robes of rank, posthumously granted his former office, and gave the posthumous title Duke Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen deeply mourned his passing, granted him a set of ceremonial robes, confirmed his former rank posthumously, and gave him the posthumous name Duke Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 長子興祖，襲爵山陽公，後例降為侯。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xingzu inherited the title Duke of Shanyang; later by precedent the title was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xingzu inherited the title of Duke of Shanyang; later, by precedent, the rank was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 景明元年卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingming he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Jingming.

sentences.zh: 興祖弟伯慶，為中散，咸陽王禧郎中令。

translations.literal: Xingzu's younger brother Boqing served as Central Attendant and Chief of the Household to the Prince of Xianyang, Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzu's younger brother Boqing served as Central Attendant and Chief of the Household to Prince Xi of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 伯慶弟世興，校書郎。

translations.literal: Boqing's younger brother Shixing served as Collator.
translations.idiomatic: Boqing's younger brother Shixing served as Collator.

sentences.zh: 羅漢弟大檀，為中散、恒農太守。

translations.literal: Luohan's younger brother Datan served as Central Attendant and Administrator of Hengnong.
translations.idiomatic: Luohan's younger brother Datan served as Central Attendant and Administrator of Hengnong.

sentences.zh: 大檀弟豹子，東萊鎮將。

translations.literal: Datan's younger brother Baozi served as Garrison Commander of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Datan's younger brother Baozi served as Garrison Commander of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 後改鎮為州，行光州事。

translations.literal: Later the garrison was changed to a province, and he acted as Administrator of Guang province.
translations.idiomatic: When the garrison was later converted to a province, he served as acting Administrator of Guang province.

sentences.zh: 豹子弟七寶，侍御中散。

translations.literal: Baozi's younger clansman Qibao served as Central Attendant of the Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi's younger clansman Qibao served as Central Attendant of the Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 遷少卿，出為假節、龍驤將軍、東雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Junior Chamberlain and went out with provisional authority as General of the Flying Dragon and Inspector of Dongyong province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Junior Chamberlain and sent out with provisional authority as General of the Flying Dragon and Inspector of Dongyong province.

sentences.zh: 孔伯恭，魏郡鄴人也。

translations.literal: Kong Bogong was a man of Ye in Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Bogong was a native of Ye in Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 父昭，始光初，以密皇后親，賜爵汝陰侯，加安東將軍，徙爵魏縣侯，遷安南將軍。

translations.literal: His father Zhao, at the beginning of Shiguang, because he was kin to the Secret Empress, was bestowed the title Marquis of Runan and given additionally the rank of General Who Pacifies the East; his title was transferred to Marquis of Wei county and he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhao, at the start of the Shiguang era, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Runan and made General Who Pacifies the East on account of his kinship with the Secret Empress; his title was later changed to Marquis of Wei county and he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 昭性柔曠，有才用。

translations.literal: Zhao's nature was gentle and open-minded; he had talent and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was gentle and broad-minded, with both talent and practical ability.

sentences.zh: 出為趙郡太守，治有能名。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Zhao commandery and in governance had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Zhao commandery and earned a reputation for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 徵拜光祿大夫，轉中都大官，善察獄訟，明於政刑。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, was transferred to Grand Master of the Central Capital, was skilled at examining prison cases and litigation, and was clear in governance and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, then transferred to Grand Master of the Central Capital. He was adept at investigating legal cases and discerning in matters of government and penal law.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、鎮東將軍、幽州刺史，進爵魯郡公。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of You Province, and advanced in rank to Duke of Lu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of You Province, and raised to Duke of Lu commandery.

sentences.zh: 和平二年卒，諡曰康公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Heping he died; his posthumous title was Duke Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Heping era and was given the posthumous title Duke Kang.

sentences.zh: 長子羅漢，東宮洗馬。

translations.literal: His eldest son Luohan served as Groom of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Luohan served as Groom of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 次伯恭，以父任拜給事中。

translations.literal: Next was Bogong, who by his father's privilege was appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The second son, Bogong, entered office through his father's privilege and was appointed Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 後賜爵濟陽男，加鷹揚將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was granted the title Baron of Jiyang and given additionally the rank of General of Flying Hawk.
translations.idiomatic: He was later enfeoffed as Baron of Jiyang and given the additional rank of General of Flying Hawk.

sentences.zh: 出為安南將軍、濟州刺史，進爵城陽公。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Ji Province, and advanced in rank to Duke of Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Ji Province, and promoted to Duke of Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 入為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He entered court as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 顯祖初，劉彧徐州刺史薛安都以彭城內附，彧遣將張永、沈攸之等擊安都，安都上表請援。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Liu Yu's Inspector of Xu Province, Xue Andu, submitted Pengcheng to Wei from within; Yu sent Generals Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi and others to attack Andu, and Andu memorialized requesting relief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Xue Andu, Liu Yu's Inspector of Xu Province, surrendered Pengcheng to Wei from within. Liu Yu sent Generals Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi and others against him, and Andu submitted a memorial requesting aid.

sentences.zh: 顯祖進伯恭號鎮東將軍，副尚書尉元救之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen advanced Bogong's title to General Who Pacifies the East and made him deputy to Minister Wei Yuan to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen promoted Bogong to General Who Pacifies the East and sent him as deputy to Minister Wei Yuan to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 軍次于秺，賊將周凱聞伯恭等軍至，棄眾遁走。

translations.literal: The army halted at Dui; the rebel general Zhou Kai, hearing that Bogong's army had arrived, abandoned his troops and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The army encamped at Dui. When the enemy general Zhou Kai learned that Bogong's forces had arrived, he abandoned his troops and fled.

sentences.zh: 張永仍屯下磕，永輜重在武原，伯恭等攻而克之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong still encamped at Xiake; Yong's baggage train was at Wuyuan, and Bogong and the others attacked and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong still held Xiake, but his supply train was at Wuyuan; Bogong and his colleagues attacked and took it.

sentences.zh: 永計無所出，引師而退。

translations.literal: Yong could think of no plan; he withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Yong could devise no countermeasure and withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 時皇興元年正月，天大寒雪，泗水冰合，永與攸之棄船而走，伯恭等進擊，首虜及凍死甚眾。

translations.literal: At that time, in the first month of the first year of Huangxing, heaven was bitterly cold with snow, the Si River froze solid, Yong and Youzhi abandoned their boats and fled on foot; Bogong and the others pressed the attack, and heads taken, captives, and those who froze to death were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: It was the first month of the first year of Huangxing, and the cold was fierce; snow fell and the Si River froze over. Yong and Youzhi abandoned their boats and fled on foot. Bogong pressed the attack, and captives, slain, and those who perished in the freeze were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 八月，伯恭以書喻下邳、宿豫城內曰：「劉彧肆逆滔天，弗鑒靈命，猶謂絕而復興，長江可恃，敢遣張永、周凱等率此蟻眾，送死彭城。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Bogong sent a letter to instruct those within Xiapi and Suyu, saying, "Liu Yu's rebellion reaches to heaven; he does not reflect on the mandate of the spirits, yet still believes that what was ended may rise again and that the Yangzi may be relied upon. He dares to send Zhang Yong, Zhou Kai, and others to lead this ant-like multitude to deliver themselves to death at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Bogong sent a letter urging the defenders of Xiapi and Suyu to submit: "Liu Yu's treason towers to the heavens. Blind to the mandate of Heaven, he still fancies that what was extinguished may live again and that the Yangzi will protect him. He dares dispatch Zhang Yong, Zhou Kai, and others at the head of this ant-swarm to throw away their lives at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 大軍未臨，逆首奔潰。

translations.literal: Before the great army had even arrived, the rebel chiefs had already fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Before our main force even arrived, the rebel leaders had already broken and fled.

sentences.zh: 今乘機電舉，當屠此城，遂平吳會，弔民伐罪。

translations.literal: Now, seizing the moment, we shall raise our banners like lightning, slaughter this city, then pacify Wu and Kuaiji, comforting the people while punishing the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Now we shall strike like lightning, take this city, pacify Wu and Kuaiji, and succor the people while punishing the guilty.

sentences.zh: 幸時歸款，自求多福。」

translations.literal: If you submit in good time, you will secure blessings for yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Submit while you still may, and choose fortune for yourselves."

sentences.zh: 時攸之、吳憘公等率眾數萬來援下邳，屯軍焦墟曲，去下邳五十餘里。

translations.literal: At that time Youzhi, Wu Xigong, and others led several tens of thousands of men to relieve Xiapi, encamping at Jiaoxu Qu, more than fifty li from Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shen Youzhi, Wu Xigong, and others were marching to relieve Xiapi with an army of tens of thousands, encamped at Jiaoxu Qu, some fifty li from the city.

sentences.zh: 伯恭遣子都將侯汾等率騎五百在水南，奚升等五百餘騎在水北，南北邀之。

translations.literal: Bogong sent Colonel of the Son's Guard Hou Fen and others to lead five hundred horsemen south of the water, and Xi Sheng and more than five hundred horsemen north of the water, to intercept them from north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Bogong sent Colonel of the Son's Guard Hou Fen with five hundred cavalry south of the river and Xi Sheng with more than five hundred cavalry north of it to block the enemy from both sides.

sentences.zh: 伯恭密造火車攻具，欲水陸俱進。

translations.literal: Bogong secretly built fire-carts and siege engines, intending to advance by both land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Bogong secretly constructed fire-carts and siege engines, planning an advance by land and water together.

sentences.zh: 攸之等既聞，將戰，引軍退保樊階城。

translations.literal: When Youzhi and the others heard of this, though they were about to give battle, they withdrew their army and held Fanjie city.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi and his colleagues learned of this, they were preparing to fight, but instead withdrew and fortified themselves at Fanjie.

sentences.zh: 伯恭又令子都將孫天慶等步騎六千向零中峽，斫木斷清水路。

translations.literal: Bogong again ordered Colonel of the Son's Guard Sun Tianqing and others with six thousand infantry and cavalry to move toward Lingzhong Gorge, felling trees to cut off the route on the Qing River.
translations.idiomatic: Bogong then sent Colonel of the Son's Guard Sun Tianqing and others with six thousand foot and horse toward Lingzhong Gorge to fell trees and block the Qing River route.

sentences.zh: 劉彧寧朔將軍陳顯達領眾二千溯清而上，以迎攸之，屯于睢清合口。

translations.literal: Liu Yu's General Who Pacifies the North, Chen Xianda, led two thousand men upstream on the Qing to meet Youzhi, and encamped at the confluence of the Sui and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's General Who Pacifies the North, Chen Xianda, led two thousand men up the Qing River to meet Youzhi and encamped where the Sui joined the Qing.

sentences.zh: 伯恭率眾渡水，大破顯達軍，俘斬十九。

translations.literal: Bogong led his troops across the water and utterly defeated Xianda's army, capturing and beheading nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: Bogong crossed the river with his troops and routed Chen Xianda's army, capturing and slaying the enemy in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 攸之聞顯達軍敗，順流退下。

translations.literal: Youzhi, hearing that Xianda's army had been defeated, retreated downstream.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi learned that Xianda's army had been broken, he withdrew downstream.

sentences.zh: 伯恭部分諸將，俠清南北尋攸之軍後。

translations.literal: Bogong assigned the various generals to press along both north and south of the Qing and pursue the rear of Youzhi's army.
translations.idiomatic: Bogong deployed his generals along both banks of the Qing to pursue Youzhi's retreating force.

sentences.zh: 伯恭從睢陵城東向零中峽，分軍為二道，遣司馬范師子等在清南，伯恭從清西，與攸之合戰，遂大破之，斬其將姜產之、高遵世及丘幼弼、丘隆先、沈榮宗、陸道景等首，攸之、憘公等輕騎遁走。

translations.literal: Bogong marched east from Suiling city toward Lingzhong Gorge, divided the army into two columns, sent Chief Clerk Fan Shizi and others on the south of the Qing while Bogong himself went by the west of the Qing, joined battle with Youzhi, and utterly defeated him; he beheaded the enemy generals Jiang Chanzi, Gao Zunshi, and Qiu Youbi, Qiu Longxian, Shen Rongzong, Lu Daojing, and others, while Youzhi, Xigong, and others fled away on light horse.
translations.idiomatic: Bogong marched east from Suiling toward Lingzhong Gorge and split his force in two: Chief Clerk Fan Shizi took the south bank of the Qing while Bogong himself advanced along the west bank. They engaged Youzhi and won a crushing victory, taking the heads of enemy generals Jiang Chanzi, Gao Zunshi, Qiu Youbi, Qiu Longxian, Shen Rongzong, Lu Daojing, and others. Youzhi, Xigong, and their companions escaped on swift mounts.

sentences.zh: 乘勝追奔八十餘里，軍資器械，虜獲萬計。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory in pursuit for more than eighty li, military supplies and weapons captured and taken numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued the fleeing enemy for more than eighty li, seizing weapons and supplies by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 進攻宿豫，劉彧戍將魯僧遵棄城夜遁。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Suyu, Liu Yu's garrison commander Lu Sengzun abandoned the city and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on to Suyu, they found Liu Yu's garrison commander Lu Sengzun had abandoned the city and fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 又遣將孔太恒等領募騎一千南討淮陽，彧太守崔武仲焚城南走，遂據淮陽。

translations.literal: He also sent General Kong Taiheng and others to lead one thousand recruited horsemen south to subdue Huaiyang; Yu's Administrator Cui Wuzhong burned the city and fled south, and they then occupied Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He also dispatched General Kong Taiheng and others with one thousand recruited cavalry to attack Huaiyang southward. Liu Yu's Administrator Cui Wuzhong set fire to the city and fled south, and Huaiyang fell to Bogong's forces.

sentences.zh: 二年，以伯恭為散騎常侍、都督徐南兗州諸軍事、鎮東將軍、彭城鎮將、東海公。

translations.literal: In the second year, Bogong was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Xu, Southern Yan, and Yan Provinces, General Who Pacifies the East, Garrison Commander of Pengcheng, and Duke of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Xu, Southern Yan, and Yan Provinces, General Who Pacifies the East, Garrison Commander of Pengcheng, and Duke of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 三年十月卒，贈鎮東大將軍、東海王，諡曰桓。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year he died; he was posthumously given the rank of Great General Who Pacifies the East and the title Prince of Donghai, with the posthumous name Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of the third year and was posthumously ennobled as Great General Who Pacifies the East and Prince of Donghai, with the posthumous name Huan.

sentences.zh: 伯恭弟伯孫，為中書□士，[9]襲父爵魯郡公。

translations.literal: Bogong's younger brother Borsun served as Central Secretariat □ Scholar, [9] and inherited his father's title Duke of Lu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Bogong's younger brother Borsun served as Central Secretariat □ Scholar, [9] and inherited their father Zhao's title as Duke of Lu commandery.

sentences.zh: 拜鎮東將軍、東萊鎮將，轉本將軍、東徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Garrison Commander of Donglai, then transferred to the same generalship and made Inspector of Eastern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Pacifies the East and Garrison Commander of Donglai, then transferred to the same rank as Inspector of Eastern Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 坐事免官，卒于家。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office for an offense and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office for an offense and died at home.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：韓茂、皮豹子、封敕文、呂羅漢、孔伯恭之為將也，皆以沉勇篤實，仁厚撫眾。

translations.literal: The historian writes: In their service as generals, Han Mao, Pi Baozi, Feng Chiwen, Lu Luohan, and Kong Bogong all alike were deep, brave, sincere, and solid, and treated their troops with benevolence and generosity.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: As commanders, Han Mao, Pi Baozi, Feng Chiwen, Lu Luohan, and Kong Bogong were alike steadfast and brave, sincere in character, and generous in their care for their troops.

sentences.zh: 功成事立，不徒然矣。

translations.literal: Their achievements were established and their tasks completed—not in vain.
translations.idiomatic: They achieved lasting success; their deeds were no empty show.

sentences.zh: 與夫苟要一戰之利，僥幸暫勝之名，豈同年而語也。

translations.literal: Compared with those who grasp only for the profit of a single battle or the name of a fleeting victory—how can they be spoken of in the same year?
translations.idiomatic: How can they be mentioned in the same breath as men who chase the profit of one battle or the empty fame of a chance victory?

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 安定安武人也 諸本「安武」作「武安」，北史卷三七韓茂傳作「安武」。

translations.literal: "A man of Anwu in Anding": in all editions "Anwu" is written "Wu'an"; Beishi juan 37 biography of Han Mao has "Anwu."
translations.idiomatic: "A man of Anwu in Anding": in all editions "Anwu" is written as "Wu'an"; the Beishi biography of Han Mao (juan 37) reads "Anwu."

sentences.zh: 按武安屬魏郡

translations.literal: According to this, Wu'an belonged to Wei commandery
translations.idiomatic: According to the Geographical Treatise, Wu'an belonged to Wei commandery

sentences.zh: 〈卷一０六上地形志上〉

translations.literal: 〈Geographical Treatise, Part One, juan 106a〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Geographical Treatise, Part One, juan 106a〉

sentences.zh: ，不屬安定；

translations.literal: , and did not belong to Anding;
translations.idiomatic: and did not belong to Anding;

sentences.zh: 安武屬豳州西北地郡。

translations.literal: Anwu belonged to Northwest Territories commandery in Bin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Anwu belonged to Northwest Territories commandery in Bin Province.

sentences.zh: 卷一０六下地形志下「安武」下注云：「前漢屬安定，後漢晉罷，後復，屬。」

translations.literal: Geographical Treatise, Part Two, juan 106b, note on "Anwu" reads: "In Former Han it belonged to Anding; in Later Han and Jin it was abolished, then restored, and belonged to [Northwest Territories]."
translations.idiomatic: The Geographical Treatise, Part Two (juan 106b), notes under "Anwu": "In Former Han it belonged to Anding; in Later Han and Jin it was abolished, then restored, and belonged to [that commandery].

sentences.zh: 這裏當是用漢代郡縣名。

translations.literal: Here the Han-dynasty commandery and county names are evidently being used.
translations.idiomatic: The text here evidently uses Han-dynasty commandery and county names.

sentences.zh: 「武安」乃「安武」倒誤，下云「假安武侯」，亦可證，今據乙。

translations.literal: "Wu'an" is the inverted error for "Anwu"; below it says "acting Marquis of Anwu," which also confirms this—now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: "Wu'an" is a transposition of "Anwu"; the passage below, "acting Marquis of Anwu," confirms this. The text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 但承仇池局人 諸本「局」下注云：「本或作『句』，或作『勾』，皆疑。」

translations.literal: "But inherited the men of Chou Pool": in all editions the note on "Pool" reads: "The original may read 'Sentence,' or 'Hook'—all doubtful."
translations.idiomatic: "But inherited the men of Chou Pool": all editions carry a note on "Pool" reading, "The original may read 'Sentence' or 'Hook'—both are uncertain."

sentences.zh: 須長

translations.literal: must wait long
translations.idiomatic: We must wait a considerable time

translations.literal: 〈Lacuna〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Lacuna〉

sentences.zh: 上邽安定戍兵至 按所闕當是「安」字。

translations.literal: Shanggui Anding garrison troops arrived: according to this, the missing character should be "An."
translations.idiomatic: Shanggui Anding garrison troops arrived: the missing character should be "An."

sentences.zh: 苦高平騎至 按「苦」當是「若」之訛。

translations.literal: Bitter Gao Ping cavalry arrived: according to this, "bitter" is the error for "if."
translations.idiomatic: "Bitter Gao Ping cavalry arrived": "bitter" is a corruption of "if."

sentences.zh: 侵掠澆河 諸本「掠」作「涼」，北史卷三七皮豹子傳作「掠」。

translations.literal: Raids on the Jiao River: in all editions "raid" is written "cool"; Beishi juan 37 biography of Pi Baozi has "raid."
translations.idiomatic: "Raids on the Jiao River": in all editions "raid" is written as "cool"; the Beishi biography of Pi Baozi (juan 37) reads "raid."

sentences.zh: 按「涼」字無義，卷一０一吐谷渾傳云：「拾寅部落大饑，屢寇澆河。」

translations.literal: According to this, the character "cool" makes no sense; juan 101, Tuyuhun biography, says: "Shibin's tribes suffered great famine and repeatedly raided the Jiao River."
translations.idiomatic: The character "cool" makes no sense. The Tuyuhun biography (juan 101) says: "Shibin's tribes suffered great famine and repeatedly raided the Jiao River.

sentences.zh: 知作「掠」是，今據北史改。

translations.literal: Thus writing "raid" is correct; now emended according to Beishi.
translations.idiomatic: Writing "raid" is therefore correct; the text is emended according to the Beishi.

sentences.zh: 又「澆」字下諸本都注云：「一作『洮』。」

translations.literal: Again, below the character "Jiao" all editions note: "One reading has 'Tao.'
translations.idiomatic: All editions also note below "Jiao": "One reading has 'Tao.'"

sentences.zh: 按澆河城見水經注卷二河水篇，吐谷渾傳及北史都作「澆河」。

translations.literal: According to this, Jiaohe city appears in Shui jing zhu, juan 2, section on the Yellow River; the Tuyuhun biography and Beishi both write "Jiao River."
translations.idiomatic: Jiaohe city appears in the commentary to the Classic of Waterways (juan 2, Yellow River section); both the Tuyuhun biography and the Beishi write "Jiao River."

sentences.zh: 隋書卷二九地理志澆河郡下注云「後周置洮河郡」，是「洮河」之名後起。

translations.literal: Suishu juan 29 Geographical Treatise, note under Jiaohe commandery, says "Later Zhou established Taohe commandery"—thus the name "Tao River" arose later.
translations.idiomatic: The Suishu Geographical Treatise (juan 29), under Jiaohe commandery, notes that "Later Zhou established Taohe commandery"—the name "Tao River" is therefore later.

sentences.zh: 這裏作「澆」是。

translations.literal: Here writing "Jiao" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Here "Jiao" is correct.

sentences.zh: 據上邽東城 北史卷三七封敕文傳「東城」下有「南城」二字。

translations.literal: Occupied the eastern city of Shanggui: Beishi juan 37 biography of Feng Chiwen has the two characters "southern city" after "eastern city."
translations.idiomatic: "Occupied the eastern city of Shanggui": in the Beishi biography of Feng Chiwen (juan 37), "eastern city" is followed by "southern city."

sentences.zh: 按下文說敕文「分兵二百人，突入南城」，知邊冏、梁會佔領上邽的東、南二城，這裏「東城」下當脫「南城」二字。

translations.literal: According to the text below, which says Chiwen "divided two hundred men to burst into the southern city," we know Bian Tong and Liang Hui occupied the eastern and southern cities of Shanggui; here the two characters "southern city" must have dropped out after "eastern city."
translations.idiomatic: The passage below states that Chiwen "sent two hundred men to burst into the southern city," showing that Bian Tong and Liang Hui held both the eastern and southern cities of Shanggui. The words "southern city" must have dropped out here after "eastern city."

sentences.zh: 討度文德 殿本考證和李慈銘都說「討」字乃「計」字之訛。

translations.literal: Calculating Wende: both the Palace edition's textual verification and Li Ciming say the character "campaign" is the error for "calculate."
translations.idiomatic: "Calculating Wende": both the Palace edition's textual verification and Li Ciming hold that "campaign" is a corruption of "calculate."

sentences.zh: 上邽休官呂豐屠各王飛廉等八千餘家 北史卷三七呂羅漢傳、冊府卷四二六

translations.literal: Shanggui Xiuguan Lu Feng, Tuge King Feilian, and more than eight thousand households: Beishi juan 37 biography of Lu Luohan and Cefu juan 426
translations.idiomatic: "Shanggui Xiuguan Lu Feng, Tuge King Feilian, and more than eight thousand households": the Beishi biography of Lu Luohan (juan 37) and Cefu (juan 426)

sentences.zh: 〈五０七六頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 5076〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈page 5076〉

translations.literal: write "Lian" as "Lu."
translations.idiomatic: write "Lian" as "Lu."

sentences.zh: 按冊府錄魏書而與北史同，疑作「鹿」是。

translations.literal: According to this, Cefu records the Book of Wei and agrees with Beishi; it is suspected that writing "Lu" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Since Cefu reproduces the Book of Wei and agrees with the Beishi, "Lu" is probably correct.

sentences.zh: 為中書□士 按所闕字當是「博」字。

translations.literal: Served as Central Secretariat □ Scholar: according to this, the missing character should be "Bo."
translations.idiomatic: "Served as Central Secretariat □ Scholar": the missing character should be "Bo."

sentences.zh: 北魏前期未設立國子學，於中書省置博士及學生。

translations.literal: In the early period of Northern Wei the Directorate of Education had not yet been established; erudites and students were placed in the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Northern Wei the Directorate of Education had not yet been established; erudites and students were instead placed within the Central Secretariat.
